tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not le… [truncated]

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

## Architecture

```text
Windows process and window metadata (exe name, PID, HWND)
  -> unique source-specific confirmed game-window selection, explicit ambiguity
  -> Windows Graphics Capture for the selected window, RGBA frame
  -> cumulative and local pixel change checks, persistently animated tiles
     suppressed (seat avatars, badges, glows), stability gate
  -> one inference worker and one replaceable latest frame
  -> generation, epoch, window identity and capture-age checks
  -> strict screen classification and complete poker-state validation
  -> two matching fresh observations and hand transition guards
  -> Monte Carlo equity and legal decision pipeline
  -> JSON-lines status, leased decision, clear, or discarded event
```

The native capture loop continues during a blocking local Laya
request. A changed or lost window, ambiguous selection, stale frame, or expired
lease clears active advice. Configured source identity and strict recognition,
quality and action validation are required before a visual recommendation. Repeated
model agreement is not independent proof of correct recognition; the held-out
real-image gate remains necessary.

The workspace crates are `ingest` (capture and vision), `core-engine` (poker math),
`ghost-layer` (unwired timing primitives), `opponent-model`, `ui` (unwired native
desktop panel), and `bin` (CLI, replay, diagnostics and evaluation). The current
browser is a local observation dashboard with no input execution layer. Observed
controls, history, calculated metrics and eventual recommendations stay separate;
legacy table events and raw model answers are not trusted current hero actions.

## CLI

From a source checkout, run these in PowerShell after following the install guide:

```powershell
cargo run --release --locked --bin coinpoker -- --help
cargo run --release --locked --bin coinpoker -- --stdin
cargo run --release --locked --bin coinpoker -- --list-windows
cargo run --release --locked --bin coinpoker -- --doctor
cargo run --release --locked --bin coinpoker -- --evaluate fixtures/synthetic/manifest.json
```

The historical source-free candidate archive supports bundled CLI/replay checks:

```powershell
& .\coinpoker.exe --help
& .\coinpoker.exe --stdin
& .\coinpoker.exe --list-windows
& .\coinpoker.exe --doctor
& .\coinpoker.exe --evaluate fixtures/synthetic/manifest.json
```

The real client executable and title conventions must come from `--list-windows` on
the actual installed client. The listing reads public metadata and may contain
personal window titles. It captures no pixels. The following low-level selector
example is internal calibration/diagnostic tooling, not a Monitor connect step:

```powershell
$env:COINPOKER_EXE_NAME = '<observed executable name>'
$env:COINPOKER_WINDOW_TITLE = '<observed table-only title fragment>'
$env:COINPOKER_LOBBY_TITLE = '<observed lobby title fragment>'
cargo run --release --locked --bin coinpoker
```

This is not the dashboard-only first-phase startup. With the current helper,
seating and play are manual; capture alone does not establish analysis eligibility.
The old candidate binary invocation is:

```powershell
& .\coinpoker.exe
```

CLI values override nonempty environment values, which override defaults. Invalid
values fail instead of being clamped. `--help` lists all timing and pixel bounds.

| CLI | Environment | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--exe-name` | `COINPOKER_EXE_NAME` | Exact calibrated executable basename, required for live discovery |
| `--pid` | `COINPOKER_PID` | Optional process pin; remove it for restart recovery |
| `--window-hwnd` | `COINPOKER_WINDOW_HWND` | Optional hexadecimal HWND pin; remove it for replacement-window recovery |
| `--table-title` | `COINPOKER_WINDOW_TITLE` | Calibrated table-only substring, required for advice |
| `--lobby-title` | `COINPOKER_LOBBY_TITLE` | Lobby veto that takes precedence over a table hint |
| `--lobby-size` | `COINPOKER_LOBBY_SIZE` | Observed lobby `WIDTHxHEIGHT`. The same title at another size is the table |
| `--vlm-endpoint` | `COINPOKER_VLM_ENDPOINT` | Sole local target: `http://127.0.0.1:18090/v1/laya/predict` |
| `--vlm-model` | `COINPOKER_VLM_MODEL` | Sole pinned alias: `coinpoker-laya-vision`; verify through `/v1/models` |
| `--timeout-secs` | `COINPOKER_VLM_TIMEOUT_SECS` | Per-request timeout, default 5 seconds; not a fresh budget for every phase |
| `--decision-budget-ms` | `COINPOKER_DECISION_BUDGET_MS` | Total source-capture deadline, default 5000 ms, bounds 500..5000; reserves 300 ms for publication/poll/render |
| `--retry-ms` | `COINPOKER_RETRY_MS` | Default 2000 ms; bounded recovery delay |

Equal-ranked windows produce an ambiguity state. A PID or HWND pin is a deliberate
restriction and will wait if its target disappears. Title strings and public process
metadata are user calibration, not cryptographic proof that a window is a table.

## Privacy and model provenance

Explicit native capture requests the selected window through Windows Graphics
Capture. The pixel boundary still needs physical evidence. Laya receives local
PNG region requests; browser snapshots/history must not expose captures, raw
model replies, backend bodies or player names. The service binds loopback only;
there is no supported remote opt-in. Keep new capture pixels under
`.local/captures/` and diagnostics private. Local logs, swap and crash dumps need
separate review; private answer logs are diagnostics, never advice inputs.

`download-model.ps1 -Verify` verifies existing Laya files against
`scripts/laya-pins.json`. Repository source is MIT; the pinned Laya fork and
upstream SmolVLM backbone are Apache-2.0, but Laya weights and the local derivative are
CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 and are not redistributed. See [model terms](MODEL_LICENSES.md)
and [compatibility evidence](docs/VLM_COMPATIBILITY.md). The orphaned
`scripts/vlm-pins.json` is historical only.

## Structured replay

`--stdin` consumes one complete `GameState` per line and retains its existing bare
decision and clear records. It does not need capture or model setup. Invalid input
clears an active recommendation once; later valid input may recover.

```json
{"game_phase":"flop","hero_cards":[{"rank":"A","suit":"spades"},{"rank":"K","suit":"hearts"}],"board":[{"rank":"A","suit":"diamonds"},{"rank":"7","suit":"clubs"},{"rank":"2","suit":"spades"}],"pot_size":1000,"to_call":500,"hero_chips":5000,"min_raise_to":1500,"max_raise_to":5000,"players":[{"name":"Hero","chips":5000,"last_action":"check","bet_amount":0},{"name":"Villain","chips":4500,"last_action":"bet","bet_amount":500}],"action_required":true,"available_actions":["fold","call","raise"]}
```

## Known limits

- Pixel checks reject malformed, blank and tiny frames; they do not positively
  identify a real table. Wrong title calibration and correlated model errors remain
  possible.
- The 8-second maximum frame age is independent of the tighter 5-second total
  deadline. Published leases use the shorter remaining limit, not a new lifetime
  from delivery. Consumers must honor invalidation, absolute expiry and EOF even
  when capture blocks.
- Persistently animated tiles (seat avatars, badges, glows) are excluded from
  change detection while they animate, so a state change inside such a tile is
  only picked up by the periodic forced refresh (5 s by default), not instantly.
  On a live six-max table real state changes arrive every few hundred
  milliseconds; an inference of several seconds rarely finds a quiet window.

# Security policy

## Reporting

Use the repository's private GitHub security-advisory flow when available, or
contact the maintainers privately. Include affected revision, reproduction, impact
and mitigation. Never attach captured tables, credentials, private model requests
or window listings to a public issue.

## Screenshot and output boundaries

Explicit native capture requests a selected window and sends local PNG region
requests to the sole Laya backend. The pixel boundary still needs physical
Windows evidence. The canonical browser/service is loopback-only at
`http://127.0.0.1:18090/`, with `/v1/models` (alias `coinpoker-laya-vision`)
and `/v1/laya/predict`. There is no supported remote opt-in, Gemma fallback,
retired product endpoint or automatic alternate port. The local listener is
unauthenticated; do not expose it through a proxy or tunnel. An occupied 18090
is a conflict, not permission to stop an unowned process.

UI/status requests must remain independent
of model loading and the single GPU admission slot, with bounded requests,
Host/Origin validation, restrictive CSP and safe text rendering. No arbitrary
file serving, raw images/model replies, backend bodies or player names belong
in browser DTOs. These are implementation-test requirements, not an accepted
live-security receipt. Session mutations use explicit requests bound to the current
service and session. Status polling does not implicitly start or stop capture.

Live decisions are scoped to an executable name, PID and HWND, plus observation
generation and expiry. Consumers must clear on `clear`, lease expiry, EOF or process
replacement; see [EVENTS_V2.md](docs/EVENTS_V2.md). Public process metadata and
configured title fragments are calibration aids, not executable authentication or
proof that a window is a poker table. Visual extraction can still be wrong.
Raw answers and legacy table events do not establish current hero controls or
eligible history. Follow-on observation invalidation/capture health must clear
current views even when no advice exists; polling cannot renew an expired lease.

Public event/browser output must exclude screenshots, PNG data URLs, raw Laya
payloads and server error bodies. Local images are not anonymized simply because
the DTO uses opaque IDs; `--list-windows` may expose personal titles. Private
answer logs are diagnostics, never advice inputs. Historical Gemma color probes
are not the current typed Laya API. Keep doctor/evaluation local, and review
local server logs, swap and crash dumps separately.

Keep new real capture pixels under ignored `.local/captures/`; existing local
fixture/label records remain private. Planned bounded per-session history under
`.local/` stores opaque session/table/seat-occupant identities and explicit gaps,
not public names, uploads or guessed cross-session merges. At a recording limit,
preserve the evidence prefix and report incomplete coverage. Demo/replay browser
requests must not start capture, write live history or trigger training.

Reuse the local `20261009T190322Z-it1` checkpoint; fresh installs lack this
user's fine-tuned derivative. Repository source is MIT; the pinned Laya fork and
upstream backbone are Apache-2.0, and Laya base/derivative weights CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0; weights
are not redistributed. Historical candidate archives omit current Laya
server/dashboard support and local weights, as well as credentials/private
fixtures/logs. The helper does not hide processes, inspect client memory,
intercept traffic or send client input.

model/temperature readiness is not quality
approval. Positive real UI data and approved human-held-out calibration/evaluation

does not turn that receipt into a pass. No confident board units at threshold
1.0 remains a failure, not a reason to clamp the threshold.

Browser, launcher and feed/ledger changes need their own actual tests. Model
health or replay success is not `COLLECTOR_READY`: measured target/timestamps,
frame progress and actual recorder/output counters must be tested. Neither
collector readiness nor temperature calibration supplies seated advice approval;
positive real UI data and approved human-held-out calibration/evaluation are
still required. The root charts/PDF are reference facts, not positive UI pixels.
Current native feed health has `recording_enabled:false`, `recorded_frames:0`;
do not treat capture-frame counters as image recording. Typed `-LiveConfig`
target settings do not add a `--record-dir` option; recorder readiness stays
at the later manual-data checkpoint.

## Toolchain and checks

The workspace pins Rust 1.95.0 in `rust-toolchain.toml`. Windows live capture also
needs the MSVC build tools and Windows SDK. Linux remains useful for structured
stdin replay and platform-neutral library checks.

These checks require a source checkout with Cargo, `scripts/validate.py` and the
test suite. Run from PowerShell before submitting a source change:

```powershell
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked
cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
python -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -v
cargo run --locked --bin coinpoker -- --evaluate fixtures/synthetic/manifest.json
python scripts/validate.py
```

`scripts/validate.py` records individual outcomes under ignored `.local/`.
Synthetic fixtures verify contracts, not real visual recognition. Capture changes
also require the physical checks in [Windows acceptance](docs/WINDOWS_ACCEPTANCE_V1.md).
Keep gates `UNRUN` until a real observation and evidence exist.

## Change rules

- Keep `Cargo.lock` committed and use `--locked` for reproducible checks.
- Keep model and server artifact identifiers, revisions and hashes consistent in
  `scripts/laya-pins.json`, `download-model.ps1`, `scripts/start-vlm.ps1`, `scripts/doctor.py`,
  [model provenance](MODEL_LICENSES.md) and
  [compatibility evidence](docs/VLM_COMPATIBILITY.md).
- Keep private images, local evaluation labels, logs and calibrated client titles
  in ignored `.local/`; new capture pixels belong under `.local/captures/`.
  Do not commit/redistribute model weights or commit `.env` files. Source/Laya
  code MIT and upstream backbone Apache-2.0 do not override CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0
  base/derivative weight constraints.
- Keep bounded private per-session history under `.local/` with opaque
  table/seat-occupant IDs, unknowns and explicit gaps; never public player names
  or cross-session identity guesses. Raw model answers and legacy table events
  are not trusted history/current-action inputs. Missing amounts are not zero.
- Preserve one-worker scheduling, fresh observation generations and epochs,
  exactly-once clearing, and leased JSON output. Add focused regression coverage
  for behavior changes and keep the protocol docs in sync. Browser polling must
  not renew old leases; invalidation must work even without active advice.
- Require a calibrated executable name and table-only title for live advice.
  Preserve the lobby veto and explicit multi-window ambiguity.
- Implement capabilities within the user's requested bug-bounty proof-of-concept
  scope. There is no repository-wide read-only restriction. Distinguish missing
  functionality from authorization restrictions; the native desktop panel remains unwired.
- `scripts/start-vlm.ps1 -DashboardOnly` is planned to load no model/use no GPU;
  default startup loads the pinned model asynchronously. Optional
  `-LiveConfig .local/profile.json` explicitly supervises one native passive
  feed, never automatic capture in this first phase. Confirm actual flag/profile
  behavior in coordinator tests before calling the instructions tested.
- Keep the historical Gate F scores/receipts and dated Gemma/port evidence.
  `scripts/vlm-pins.json` is an orphaned historical manifest, not an active pin
  source. Laya server/dashboard support and the user's local fine-tuned weights
  are omitted from historical packaging; this phase does not edit releases or
  workflows to hide that gap.

The candidate workflow can package and optionally sign an archive. A build or CI
pass does not change the physical acceptance status or version `0.1.0`.

===== SECURITY.md =====
# Security policy

## Reporting

Use the repository's private GitHub security-advisory flow when available, or
contact the maintainers privately. Include affected revision, reproduction, impact
and mitigation. Never attach captured tables, credentials, private model requests
or window listings to a public issue.

## Screenshot and output boundaries

Explicit native capture requests a selected window and sends local PNG region
requests to the sole Laya backend. The pixel boundary still needs physical
Windows evidence. The canonical browser/service is loopback-only at
`http://127.0.0.1:18090/`, with `/v1/models` (alias `coinpoker-laya-vision`)
and `/v1/laya/predict`. There is no supported remote opt-in, Gemma fallback,
retired product endpoint or automatic alternate port. The local listener is
unauthenticated; do not expose it through a proxy or tunnel. An occupied 18090
is a conflict, not permission to stop an unowned process.

UI/status requests must remain independent
of model loading and the single GPU admission slot, with bounded requests,
Host/Origin validation, restrictive CSP and safe text rendering. No arbitrary
file serving, raw images/model replies, backend bodies or player names belong
in browser DTOs. These are implementation-test requirements, not an accepted
live-security receipt. Session mutations use explicit requests bound to the current
service and session. Status polling does not implicitly start or stop capture.

Live decisions are scoped to an executable name, PID and HWND, plus observation
generation and expiry. Consumers must clear on `clear`, lease expiry, EOF or process
replacement; see [EVENTS_V2.md](docs/EVENTS_V2.md). Public process metadata and
configured title fragments are calibration aids, not executable authentication or
proof that a window is a poker table. Visual extraction can still be wrong.
Raw answers and legacy table events do not establish current hero controls or
eligible history. Follow-on observation invalidation/capture health must clear
current views even when no advice exists; polling cannot renew an expired lease.

Public event/browser output must exclude screenshots, PNG data URLs, raw Laya
payloads and server error bodies. Local images are not anonymized simply because
the DTO uses opaque IDs; `--list-windows` may expose personal titles. Private
answer logs are diagnostics, never advice inputs. Historical Gemma color probes
are not the current typed Laya API. Keep doctor/evaluation local, and review
local server logs, swap and crash dumps separately.

Keep new real capture pixels under ignored `.local/captures/`; existing local
fixture/label records remain private. Planned bounded per-session history under
`.local/` stores opaque session/table/seat-occupant identities and explicit gaps,
not public names, uploads or guessed cross-session merges. At a recording limit,
preserve the evidence prefix and report incomplete coverage. Demo/replay browser
requests must not start capture, write live history or trigger training.

Reuse the local `20261009T190322Z-it1` checkpoint; fresh installs lack this
user's fine-tuned derivative. Repository source is MIT; the pinned Laya fork and
upstream backbone are Apache-2.0, and Laya base/derivative weights CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0; weights
are not redistributed. Historical candidate archives omit current Laya
server/dashboard support and local weights, as well as credentials/private
fixtures/logs. The helper does not hide processes, inspect client memory,
intercept traffic or send client input.

The project is a user-directed bug-bounty proof of concept. Gate F remains FAIL;
model/temperature readiness is not quality
approval. Positive real UI data and approved human-held-out calibration/evaluation
are required before seated advice. The proposed 5-second full end-to-end budget
does not retroactively pass the original 3.0273-second/<2-second failed benchmark.

## Supported versions

Until versioned releases exist, security fixes target the latest revision of the
default branch.

# Hybrid Rust/Python Architecture Simplification Plan

## 1. Goal & Architectural Findings

Simplify the hybrid Rust/Python codebase by unifying duplicated geometry/region configuration, factoring internal modules in `scripts/laya-server.py`, and consolidating shared session/receipt/test boundaries in `bin/` without changing any external CLI, HTTP API, or test behavior.

### Validated Codebase Boundaries (vs. Initial Assumptions)
1. **Runtime Python Coupling**:
   - `scripts/laya-server.py` imports `laya_dashboard` and `laya_capture` at module load time, and `laya_dashboard.ManualSessionFeed.__init__` (used in `serve` mode) instantiates `laya_visual.VisualWorker`, which transitively imports `laya_board`, `laya_actions`, `laya_showdown`, `laya_numeric`, `laya_context`, `laya_evidence`, and `laya_prep`.
   - Over 20 test modules under `scripts/tests/` import `laya_*.py` directly from `scripts/` and resolve `ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]`. Therefore, existing top-level module paths in `scripts/` must remain intact.
2. **Supervisor/Child Split (`laya_capture.py` vs. `bin/manual_capture.rs`)**:
   - `scripts/laya_capture.py` (with `laya_attach.py`) is the parent supervisor that confirms windows, writes `.local/laya/manual-capture/<session_id>/approval.json`, manages `active.lock` / `status.json` / `STOP` / `run.json` / `summary.json`, and spawns `coinpoker --capture-only` or `coinpoker --manual-inference` (`bin/manual_capture.rs` and `bin/manual_inference.rs`). Both sides are required.
3. **Existing Hygiene & Manifests**:
   - `.gitignore` already excludes `/.conda/`, `/.local/`, `__pycache__/`, and `*.pyc`.
   - `scripts/vlm-pins.json` is still referenced by `.github/workflows/release-windows.yml` and documented as a retained historical manifest, so it must not be deleted.

---

## 2. Ordered Implementation Tasks

### Phase 1: Unify Geometry & Region Configuration (`regions.json` Single Source of Truth)

**Files**:
- `crates/ingest/assets/laya/regions.json` (canonical source, read-only)
- `scripts/laya_prep.py`
- `scripts/laya_visual.py`
- `scripts/laya_numeric.py`
- `crates/ingest/src/laya/geometry.rs`
- `scripts/tests/test_laya_board.py` (or dedicated geometry parity test in `scripts/tests/test_laya_server.py`)

**Steps**:
1. **Centralize `regions.json` loading in `scripts/laya_prep.py`**:
   - Add `REGIONS_REL_PATH = "crates/ingest/assets/laya/regions.json"` and a stdlib-only helper `load_regions(root=None)` in `scripts/laya_prep.py` that loads and parses `crates/ingest/assets/laya/regions.json` (using `functools.lru_cache` when `root is None`, and resolving relative to `Path(root)` when a custom root is supplied).
   - Derive `TITLE_BAR_PX`, `TITLE_BAR_RANGE`, and `CONTENT_ASPECT` in `scripts/laya_prep.py` from `load_regions()["geometry"]` (`title_bar_px`, `tuple(title_bar_range_px)`, `content_aspect`) while keeping those module-level constant names exported for backward compatibility.
   - Add `region_px(name, w, h, *, regions=None)` in `scripts/laya_prep.py` mirroring `crates/ingest/src/laya/geometry.rs::region_px`.
   - Keep `numpy` and `PIL` imports strictly lazy inside `_text_score`, `_text_mask`, `_components`, and `segment_glyphs` so importing `laya_prep` for geometry remains stdlib-only.
2. **Reuse `laya_prep.load_regions` across Python consumers**:
   - Update `scripts/laya_visual.py` (`VisualWorker._load`) and `scripts/laya_numeric.py` (`NumericReader.__init__`) to call `laya_prep.load_regions(self.root)` instead of duplicating raw `(self.root / "crates/ingest/assets/laya/regions.json").read_bytes()` JSON loads.
3. **Add cross-language Rust/Python geometry parity coverage**:
   - Expand `crates/ingest/src/laya/geometry.rs` tests and Python unit tests to verify identical `(x0, y0, cw, ch)` and `box_px` outputs across all 20 named regions in `regions.json` and across standard, letterboxed, pillarboxed, tiny, and `.5` half-to-even tie dimensions (e.g., dimensions where `w / content_aspect` or `avail_h * content_aspect` lands near `.5`).

---

### Phase 2: Internal Modularization of `scripts/laya-server.py`

**Files**:
- `scripts/laya-server.py`
- `scripts/laya_server_validation.py` (new internal helper module)
- `scripts/tests/test_laya_server.py`

**Constraints & Test Contracts to Preserve**:
- `scripts/tests/test_laya_server.py` and `scripts/tests/test_laya_dashboard.py` load `scripts/laya-server.py` via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` and access/patch module attributes on `srv`:
  - `srv.ROOT`, `srv.REPO`, `srv.HOST`, `srv.PORT`, `srv.PNG_SIG`, `srv.MAX_BODY`, `srv.MAX_READOUT_QUESTIONS`, `srv.MAX_ACCEPTANCE_REPORT`
  - `srv.ACCEPTANCE_PASSES`, `srv.STACK_PASSES`, `srv.WAGER_PASSES`, `srv.SCENE_PASSES`, `srv.WAGER_NOTE`, `srv.SCENE_NOTE`, `srv.EXPERIMENTAL_WAGER_NOTE`, `srv.EXPERIMENTAL_CHECKPOINT`, `srv.EXPERIMENTAL_MODEL_SHA256`, `srv.EXPERIMENTAL_BOUNDS`, `srv.SCENE_QUESTIONS`
  - `srv.RequestError`, `srv.load_pins`, `srv.png_size`, `srv.validate_request`, `srv.shape_answers`, `srv.answer_diagnostics`, `srv.wager_questions`, `srv.readout_core_template`
  - `srv.load_acceptance_floors`, `srv.load_seat_registry`, `srv.load_wager_registry`, `srv.load_scene_registry`, `srv.pinned_file_entries`, `srv.experimental_descriptor`, `srv.load_experimental_metadata`
  - `srv.Engine`, `srv.Service`, `srv.BoundedHTTPServer`, `srv.make_handler`, `srv.handle_predict`, `srv.handle_predict_batch`, `srv.verify`, `srv.cmd_verify`, `srv.cmd_fetch`, `srv.cmd_serve`, `srv.main`

**Steps**:
1. **Extract pure request/protocol validation & diagnostics into `scripts/laya_server_validation.py`**:
   - Move protocol constants (`MAX_*`, `ID_RE`, `LAYOUTS`, `GLYPH_STYLES`, `PNG_SIG`, `ACCEPTANCE_PASSES`, `STACK_PASSES`, `WAGER_PASSES`, `SCENE_PASSES`, `WAGER_NOTE`, `SCENE_NOTE`, `EXPERIMENTAL_*`, `SCENE_QUESTIONS`), `RequestError`, `png_size`, `validate_request`, `shape_answers`, `answer_diagnostics`, `pinned_file_entries`, and `experimental_descriptor` into `scripts/laya_server_validation.py` (stdlib-only, zero heavy imports).
   - For filesystem-bound loaders (`load_acceptance_floors`, `load_seat_registry`, `load_experimental_metadata`, `wager_questions`, `readout_core_template`), accept explicit `root` / `repo` parameters in `laya_server_validation.py` and keep thin wrappers in `scripts/laya-server.py` that pass `srv.ROOT` / `srv.REPO` so `patch.object(srv, "ROOT", ...)` and `patch.object(srv, "REPO", ...)` in `test_laya_server.py` continue to work identically.
2. **Deduplicate `handle_predict` and `handle_predict_batch` decode/glyph-prep helpers**:
   - Extract shared image decode + glyph segmentation + question filtering logic used by both `handle_predict` and `handle_predict_batch` into a single internal helper `_decode_and_prepare_pass(engine, layout, style, raw, questions)` so single and batch prediction paths do not duplicate decode/segmentation error handling.
3. **Re-export all public/tested symbols in `scripts/laya-server.py`**:
   - Import and expose every constant, exception, and helper in `scripts/laya-server.py` so external callers and `test_laya_server.py` / `test_laya_dashboard.py` require zero test modifications.

---

### Phase 3: Factor Shared Rust `bin/` Session Helpers & Inline Test Modules

**Files**:
- `bin/manual_capture.rs`
- `bin/manual_inference.rs`
- `bin/live.rs`
- `bin/manual_capture/tests.rs` (or `#[path = ...]` submodule if extracted)
- `bin/manual_inference/tests.rs`
- `bin/live/tests.rs`

**Steps**:
1. **Consolidate shared manual session receipt & source-matching helpers in `bin/manual_capture.rs`**:
   - Extract a shared helper in `bin/manual_capture.rs` for computing `recording_end_reason` + base `manual_capture` status JSON fields (`elapsed_ms`, `stop_reason`, `recording_end_reason`, `recording`, `capture_failures`, `capture_directory`, `latest_frame`, `updated_at_unix_ms`) used by both `manual_capture::emit_status` and `manual_inference::ManualSource::progress`.
   - Extract a shared single-window discovery matcher (`find_approved_window(windows: &[WindowInfo], approved: &WindowInfo) -> Option<&WindowInfo>`) used by both `manual_capture::capture_loop` and `manual_inference::ManualSource::current_window`.
2. **Split oversized inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` out of `bin/` production files**:
   - `bin/manual_inference.rs` is 3,504 lines (2,500+ lines of tests starting at line 1001), `bin/live.rs` is 2,189 lines (1,277 lines of tests starting at line 912), and `bin/manual_capture.rs` is 808 lines (381 lines of tests starting at line 426).

name: Prepare Windows candidate

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sign:
        description: Sign the candidate executable with configured Authenticode secrets
        type: boolean
        default: false

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  candidate:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - name: Install pinned Rust
        run: rustup toolchain install 1.95.0 --profile minimal --component rustfmt --component clippy
      - name: Validate candidate source
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          cargo +1.95.0 fmt --all -- --check
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Rust formatting failed' }
          cargo +1.95.0 check --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Rust check failed' }
          cargo +1.95.0 test --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Rust tests failed' }
          cargo +1.95.0 clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Clippy failed' }
          python -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -v
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Python tests failed' }
          $paths = @((Resolve-Path 'download-model.ps1').Path) + @(Get-ChildItem scripts -Filter '*.ps1' -File | ForEach-Object FullName)
          foreach ($path in $paths) {
            $tokens = $null
            $errors = $null
            [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile($path, [ref]$tokens, [ref]$errors) | Out-Null
            if ($errors.Count -gt 0) { throw "PowerShell syntax errors in $path`: $($errors -join '; ')" }
          }
          cargo +1.95.0 build --release --locked --bin coinpoker
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Release build failed' }
          & .\target\release\coinpoker.exe --evaluate fixtures/synthetic/manifest.json
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Synthetic evaluation failed' }
      - name: Stage explicit candidate allowlist
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $bundle = 'dist/coinpoker-help'
          if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $bundle) {
            throw "Candidate staging directory already exists: $bundle. Use a clean workspace so no stale files enter the archive."
          }
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $bundle | Out-Null
          $files = @(
            @{ from = 'target/release/coinpoker.exe'; to = 'coinpoker.exe' }
            @{ from = 'README.md'; to = 'README.md' }
            @{ from = 'CONTRIBUTING.md'; to = 'CONTRIBUTING.md' }
            @{ from = 'SECURITY.md'; to = 'SECURITY.md' }
            @{ from = 'LICENSE'; to = 'LICENSE' }
            @{ from = 'MODEL_LICENSES.md'; to = 'MODEL_LICENSES.md' }
            @{ from = 'download-model.ps1'; to = 'download-model.ps1' }
            @{ from = 'docs/INSTALL_WINDOWS.md'; to = 'docs/INSTALL_WINDOWS.md' }
            @{ from = 'docs/WINDOWS_ACCEPTANCE_V1.md'; to = 'docs/WINDOWS_ACCEPTANCE_V1.md' }
            @{ from = 'docs/VLM_COMPATIBILITY.md'; to = 'docs/VLM_COMPATIBILITY.md' }
            @{ from = 'docs/VISUAL_EVALUATION_V2.md'; to = 'docs/VISUAL_EVALUATION_V2.md' }
            @{ from = 'docs/EVENTS_V2.md'; to = 'docs/EVENTS_V2.md' }
            @{ from = 'scripts/doctor.py'; to = 'scripts/doctor.py' }
            @{ from = 'scripts/setup-windows.ps1'; to = 'scripts/setup-windows.ps1' }
            @{ from = 'scripts/start-vlm.ps1'; to = 'scripts/start-vlm.ps1' }
            @{ from = 'scripts/vlm-pins.json'; to = 'scripts/vlm-pins.json' }
            @{ from = 'scripts/windows-acceptance.ps1'; to = 'scripts/windows-acceptance.ps1' }
            @{ from = 'fixtures/synthetic/manifest.json'; to = 'fixtures/synthetic/manifest.json' }
          )
          foreach ($file in $files) {
            if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $file.from -PathType Leaf)) { throw "Missing allowlisted file: $($file.from)" }
            $destination = Join-Path $bundle $file.to
            New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Split-Path $destination -Parent) | Out-Null
            Copy-Item -LiteralPath $file.from -Destination $destination
          }
          'Candidate only. Physical Windows acceptance and real-image accuracy have not been established by this workflow.' |
            Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $bundle 'CANDIDATE.txt') -Encoding UTF8
          if (Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $bundle -Recurse -File | Where-Object { $_.Name -match '\.pyc$|^__pycache__$' }) {
            throw 'Private/generated files entered candidate bundle'
          }
      - name: Optional Authenticode signature
        if: ${{ inputs.sign }}
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          CERTIFICATE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.WINDOWS_SIGNING_CERTIFICATE_BASE64 }}
          CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.WINDOWS_SIGNING_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          if (-not $env:CERTIFICATE_BASE64 -or -not $env:CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD) {
            throw 'Signing requested but WINDOWS_SIGNING_CERTIFICATE_BASE64 or WINDOWS_SIGNING_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD is missing'
          }
          $kit = Join-Path ${env:ProgramFiles(x86)} 'Windows Kits/10/bin'
          $signTool = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $kit -Filter signtool.exe -Recurse -File |
            Where-Object { $_.FullName -match '[\\/]x64[\\/]signtool\.exe$' } |
            Sort-Object FullName -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
          if (-not $signTool) { throw 'Windows SDK SignTool not found' }
          $pfx = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'coinpoker-candidate.pfx'
          try {
            [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes($pfx, [Convert]::FromBase64String($env:CERTIFICATE_BASE64))
            & $signTool.FullName sign /f $pfx /p $env:CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD /fd SHA256 'dist/coinpoker-help/coinpoker.exe'
            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Authenticode signing failed' }
            $signature = Get-AuthenticodeSignature 'dist/coinpoker-help/coinpoker.exe'
            if ($signature.Status -ne 'Valid') { throw "Signed candidate verification failed: $($signature.Status)" }
          } finally {
            Remove-Item -LiteralPath $pfx -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
          }
      - name: Archive and checksum
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $archive = 'dist/coinpoker-help-windows-x64-candidate.zip'
          Compress-Archive -LiteralPath 'dist/coinpoker-help' -DestinationPath $archive -Force
          $hash = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $archive -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
          "$hash  coinpoker-help-windows-x64-candidate.zip" |
            Set-Content -LiteralPath 'dist/SHA256SUMS' -Encoding ascii
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: coinpoker-help-windows-x64-candidate
          path: |
            dist/coinpoker-help-windows-x64-candidate.zip
            dist/SHA256SUMS
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

===== .kilo plan =====
# Hybrid Rust/Python Architecture Simplification Plan

## 1. Goal & Architectural Findings

Simplify the hybrid Rust/Python codebase by unifying duplicated geometry/region configuration, factoring internal modules in `scripts/laya-server.py`, and consolidating shared session/receipt/test boundaries in `bin/` without changing any external CLI, HTTP API, or test behavior.

### Validated Codebase Boundaries (vs. Initial Assumptions)
1. **Runtime Python Coupling**:
   - `scripts/laya-server.py` imports `laya_dashboard` and `laya_capture` at module load time, and `laya_dashboard.ManualSessionFeed.__init__` (used in `serve` mode) instantiates `laya_visual.VisualWorker`, which transitively imports `laya_board`, `laya_actions`, `laya_showdown`, `laya_numeric`, `laya_context`, `laya_evidence`, and `laya_prep`.
   - Over 20 test modules under `scripts/tests/` import `laya_*.py` directly from `scripts/` and resolve `ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]`. Therefore, existing top-level module paths in `scripts/` must remain intact.
2. **Supervisor/Child Split (`laya_capture.py` vs. `bin/manual_capture.rs`)**:
   - `scripts/laya_capture.py` (with `laya_attach.py`) is the parent supervisor that confirms windows, writes `.local/laya/manual-capture/<session_id>/approval.json`, manages `active.lock` / `status.json` / `STOP` / `run.json` / `summary.json`, and spawns `coinpoker --capture-only` or `coinpoker --manual-inference` (`bin/manual_capture.rs` and `bin/manual_inference.rs`). Both sides are required.
3. **Existing Hygiene & Manifests**:
   - `.gitignore` already excludes `/.conda/`, `/.local/`, `__pycache__/`, and `*.pyc`.
   - `scripts/vlm-pins.json` is still referenced by `.github/workflows/release-windows.yml` and documented as a retained historical manifest, so it must not be deleted.

---

## 2. Ordered Implementation Tasks

### Phase 1: Unify Geometry & Region Configuration (`regions.json` Single Source of Truth)

**Files**:
- `crates/ingest/assets/laya/regions.json` (canonical source, read-only)
- `scripts/laya_prep.py`
- `scripts/laya_visual.py`
- `scripts/laya_numeric.py`
- `crates/ingest/src/laya/geometry.rs`
- `scripts/tests/test_laya_board.py` (or dedicated geometry parity test in `scripts/tests/test_laya_server.py`)

**Steps**:
1. **Centralize `regions.json` loading in `scripts/laya_prep.py`**:
   - Add `REGIONS_REL_PATH = "crates/ingest/assets/laya/regions.json"` and a stdlib-only helper `load_regions(root=None)` in `scripts/laya_prep.py` that loads and parses `crates/ingest/assets/laya/regions.json` (using `functools.lru_cache` when `root is None`, and resolving relative to `Path(root)` when a custom root is supplied).
   - Derive `TITLE_BAR_PX`, `TITLE_BAR_RANGE`, and `CONTENT_ASPECT` in `scripts/laya_prep.py` from `load_regions()["geometry"]` (`title_bar_px`, `tuple(title_bar_range_px)`, `content_aspect`) while keeping those module-level constant names exported for backward compatibility.
   - Add `region_px(name, w, h, *, regions=None)` in `scripts/laya_prep.py` mirroring `crates/ingest/src/laya/geometry.rs::region_px`.
   - Keep `numpy` and `PIL` imports strictly lazy inside `_text_score`, `_text_mask`, `_components`, and `segment_glyphs` so importing `laya_prep` for geometry remains stdlib-only.
2. **Reuse `laya_prep.load_regions` across Python consumers**:
   - Update `scripts/laya_visual.py` (`VisualWorker._load`) and `scripts/laya_numeric.py` (`NumericReader.__init__`) to call `laya_prep.load_regions(self.root)` instead of duplicating raw `(self.root / "crates/ingest/assets/laya/regions.json").read_bytes()` JSON loads.
3. **Add cross-language Rust/Python geometry parity coverage**:
   - Expand `crates/ingest/src/laya/geometry.rs` tests and Python unit tests to verify identical `(x0, y0, cw, ch)` and `box_px` outputs across all 20 named regions in `regions.json` and across standard, letterboxed, pillarboxed, tiny, and `.5` half-to-even tie dimensions (e.g., dimensions where `w / content_aspect` or `avail_h * content_aspect` lands near `.5`).

---

**Files**:
- `scripts/laya-server.py`
- `scripts/laya_server_validation.py` (new internal helper module)
- `scripts/tests/test_laya_server.py`

**Constraints & Test Contracts to Preserve**:

  - `srv.ACCEPTANCE_PASSES`, `srv.STACK_PASSES`, `srv.WAGER_PASSES`, `srv.SCENE_PASSES`, `srv.WAGER_NOTE`, `srv.SCENE_NOTE`, `srv.EXPERIMENTAL_WAGER_NOTE`, `srv.EXPERIMENTAL_CHECKPOINT`, `srv.EXPERIMENTAL_MODEL_SHA256`, `srv.EXPERIMENTAL_BOUNDS`, `srv.SCENE_QUESTIONS`
  - `srv.RequestError`, `srv.load_pins`, `srv.png_size`, `srv.validate_request`, `srv.shape_answers`, `srv.answer_diagnostics`, `srv.wager_questions`, `srv.readout_core_template`

- `bin/manual_inference.rs`
- `bin/live.rs`
- `bin/manual_capture/tests.rs` (or `#[path = ...]` submodule if extracted)

jobs:

----- .github/workflows/release-windows.yml -----
name: Prepare Windows candidate

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sign:
        description: Sign the candidate executable with configured Authenticode secrets
        type: boolean
        default: false

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  candidate:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - name: Install pinned Rust
        run: rustup toolchain install 1.95.0 --profile minimal --component rustfmt --component clippy
      - name: Validate candidate source
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          cargo +1.95.0 fmt --all -- --check
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Rust formatting failed' }
          cargo +1.95.0 check --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Rust check failed' }
          cargo +1.95.0 test --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Rust tests failed' }
          cargo +1.95.0 clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Clippy failed' }
          python -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -v
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Python tests failed' }
          $paths = @((Resolve-Path 'download-model.ps1').Path) + @(Get-ChildItem scripts -Filter '*.ps1' -File | ForEach-Object FullName)
          foreach ($path in $paths) {
            $tokens = $null
            $errors = $null
            [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile($path, [ref]$tokens, [ref]$errors) | Out-Null
            if ($errors.Count -gt 0) { throw "PowerShell syntax errors in $path`: $($errors -join '; ')" }
          }
          cargo +1.95.0 build --release --locked --bin coinpoker
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Release build failed' }
          & .\target\release\coinpoker.exe --evaluate fixtures/synthetic/manifest.json
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Synthetic evaluation failed' }
      - name: Stage explicit candidate allowlist
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $bundle = 'dist/coinpoker-help'
          if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $bundle) {
            throw "Candidate staging directory already exists: $bundle. Use a clean workspace so no stale files enter the archive."
          }
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $bundle | Out-Null
          $files = @(
            @{ from = 'target/release/coinpoker.exe'; to = 'coinpoker.exe' }
            @{ from = 'README.md'; to = 'README.md' }
            @{ from = 'CONTRIBUTING.md'; to = 'CONTRIBUTING.md' }
            @{ from = 'SECURITY.md'; to = 'SECURITY.md' }
            @{ from = 'LICENSE'; to = 'LICENSE' }
            @{ from = 'MODEL_LICENSES.md'; to = 'MODEL_LICENSES.md' }
            @{ from = 'download-model.ps1'; to = 'download-model.ps1' }
            @{ from = 'docs/INSTALL_WINDOWS.md'; to = 'docs/INSTALL_WINDOWS.md' }
            @{ from = 'docs/WINDOWS_ACCEPTANCE_V1.md'; to = 'docs/WINDOWS_ACCEPTANCE_V1.md' }
            @{ from = 'docs/VLM_COMPATIBILITY.md'; to = 'docs/VLM_COMPATIBILITY.md' }
            @{ from = 'docs/VISUAL_EVALUATION_V2.md'; to = 'docs/VISUAL_EVALUATION_V2.md' }
            @{ from = 'docs/EVENTS_V2.md'; to = 'docs/EVENTS_V2.md' }
            @{ from = 'scripts/doctor.py'; to = 'scripts/doctor.py' }
            @{ from = 'scripts/setup-windows.ps1'; to = 'scripts/setup-windows.ps1' }
            @{ from = 'scripts/start-vlm.ps1'; to = 'scripts/start-vlm.ps1' }
            @{ from = 'scripts/vlm-pins.json'; to = 'scripts/vlm-pins.json' }
            @{ from = 'scripts/windows-acceptance.ps1'; to = 'scripts/windows-acceptance.ps1' }
            @{ from = 'fixtures/synthetic/manifest.json'; to = 'fixtures/synthetic/manifest.json' }
          )
          foreach ($file in $files) {
            if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $file.from -PathType Leaf)) { throw "Missing allowlisted file: $($file.from)" }
            $destination = Join-Path $bundle $file.to
            New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Split-Path $destination -Parent) | Out-Null
            Copy-Item -LiteralPath $file.from -Destination $destination
          }
          'Candidate only. Physical Windows acceptance and real-image accuracy have not been established by this workflow.' |
            Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $bundle 'CANDIDATE.txt') -Encoding UTF8
          if (Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $bundle -Recurse -File | Where-Object { $_.Name -match '\.pyc$|^__pycache__$' }) {
            throw 'Private/generated files entered candidate bundle'
          }
      - name: Optional Authenticode signature
        if: ${{ inputs.sign }}
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          CERTIFICATE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.WINDOWS_SIGNING_CERTIFICATE_BASE64 }}
          CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.WINDOWS_SIGNING_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          if (-not $env:CERTIFICATE_BASE64 -or -not $env:CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD) {
            throw 'Signing requested but WINDOWS_SIGNING_CERTIFICATE_BASE64 or WINDOWS_SIGNING_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD is missing'
          }
          $kit = Join-Path ${env:ProgramFiles(x86)} 'Windows Kits/10/bin'
          $signTool = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $kit -Filter signtool.exe -Recurse -File |
            Where-Object { $_.FullName -match '[\\/]x64[\\/]signtool\.exe$' } |
            Sort-Object FullName -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
          if (-not $signTool) { throw 'Windows SDK SignTool not found' }
          $pfx = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'coinpoker-candidate.pfx'
          try {
            [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes($pfx, [Convert]::FromBase64String($env:CERTIFICATE_BASE64))
            & $signTool.FullName sign /f $pfx /p $env:CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD /fd SHA256 'dist/coinpoker-help/coinpoker.exe'
            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Authenticode signing failed' }
            $signature = Get-AuthenticodeSignature 'dist/coinpoker-help/coinpoker.exe'
            if ($signature.Status -ne 'Valid') { throw "Signed candidate verification failed: $($signature.Status)" }
          } finally {
            Remove-Item -LiteralPath $pfx -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
          }
      - name: Archive and checksum
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $archive = 'dist/coinpoker-help-windows-x64-candidate.zip'
          Compress-Archive -LiteralPath 'dist/coinpoker-help' -DestinationPath $archive -Force
          $hash = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $archive -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
          "$hash  coinpoker-help-windows-x64-candidate.zip" |
            Set-Content -LiteralPath 'dist/SHA256SUMS' -Encoding ascii
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: coinpoker-help-windows-x64-candidate
          path: |
            dist/coinpoker-help-windows-x64-candidate.zip
            dist/SHA256SUMS
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

1	===== README.md =====
2	# coinpoker-help
3	
4	Local bug-bounty proof of concept for poker observation and decision support.
5	Native capture targets Windows 10 version 1903 or later. Structured JSON replay
6	and poker libraries also run on Linux.
7	The current helper has no mouse/keyboard input path, client-memory reader, or
8	client-network interception.
9	
10	**Status:** engineering candidate, version `0.1.0`; Laya iteration-1 Gate F
11	**FAIL**, human verification **UNVERIFIED**, no validated live seated advice. A build,
12	synthetic evaluation or loaded model is not real-table acceptance. Physical
13	Windows, model, real-image and clean-account evidence is recorded in
14	[the Windows report](docs/WINDOWS_ACCEPTANCE_V1.md); unrun gates stay `UNRUN`.
15	Practice and cash use this same repo, representation and validation mechanism,
16	without a practice-only bypass. No real-money acceptance has been established.
17	
18	## Start here
19	
20	- [First manual seated diagnostic: launch, confirm, stop and checklist](docs/SEATED_DIAGNOSTIC.md)
21	- [Windows setup and local dashboard](docs/INSTALL_WINDOWS.md)
22	- [VLM compatibility and provenance](docs/VLM_COMPATIBILITY.md)
23	- [Live JSON-lines contract](docs/EVENTS_V2.md)
24	- [Visual evaluation contract](docs/VISUAL_EVALUATION_V2.md)
25	- [Model terms](MODEL_LICENSES.md), [security](SECURITY.md), [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)
26	
27	## Current model and browser
28	
29	The sole perception backend is Laya Vision. Reuse the already downloaded and
30	trained checkpoint `models/laya-vision/finetuned/20261009T190322Z-it1`, based on
31	`thaitea/laya-vision@f2fe3c12cb6d04c59d8a190250bf3fb40fc828dc` and recorded in
32	`scripts/laya-pins.json`. No redownload, retraining or new dump is needed for
33	this dashboard phase. A fresh install lacks this user's local fine-tuned weights.
34	
35	The canonical browser address is **`http://127.0.0.1:18090/`**. Model metadata
36	is at `/v1/models` under alias `coinpoker-laya-vision`; typed Laya requests use
37	`/v1/laya/predict` on the same listener. Gemma, ports `18080`/`8080`,
38	chat-completions and remote VLM opt-in are retired product instructions, not
39	alternate endpoints or fallbacks.
40	
41	The browser has exactly two views, **Monitor** and **Reference** in a compact
42	landscape companion. Monitor shows source/role/freshness, independent readings,
43	six physical seats and a separate recorder status; history and diagnostics are
44	collapsible. A genuine current full native observation and matching decision can
45	display **EXPERIMENTAL** analysis with `quality_approved:false`; partial readouts
46	cannot supply it. The pinned model's R17 and untrained hero/control limitations
47	remain, and no live seated capability or quality certification is claimed.
48	Reference uses a searchable topic list and selected content, with the existing
49	bundled education and citations unchanged.
50	It makes no runtime content requests and does not copy the root charts.
51	
52	Open `http://127.0.0.1:18090/` beside the selected table. **Stop capture** requests
53	termination of the current source session through the service-bound local
54	`POST /api/capture/stop`; it does not need a loaded model. There are currently no
55	HTTP start/mark, seating or betting controls. For development startup, choose
56	one mode below, not two concurrent servers; inspect the existing 18090 listener
57	before starting anything. Reuse an already running service.
58	
59	```powershell
60	# Dashboard-only startup without loading a model or using the GPU.
61	pwsh -File scripts/start-vlm.ps1 -DashboardOnly
62	```
63	
64	```powershell
65	# Normal startup is also dashboard-only. No automatic model load or attachment.
66	pwsh -File scripts/start-vlm.ps1
67	```
68	
69	The role display follows explicit current-source evidence: **Observing**,
70	**Seated** ("Waiting for your turn"), **Your turn**, or **Reading uncertain**.
71	Observing call cost/pot odds belong to the labelled acting seat, never a fictitious
72	"your call". Sitting down changes the role, not the stream or accumulated history.
73	Unknown readings stay unknown; a missing feed is one compact message, not a grid
74	of unavailable fields. Expiry, heartbeat loss, hidden/resumed tabs and disconnects
75	clear current readings without renewing their leases. Runtime/lease/ledger details
76	and synthetic fixtures stay behind the scenes, not in extra app views.
77	
78	Normal startup no longer follows a saved selector. `-LiveConfig`, a supplied
79	`-PracticeConfig` without explicit automatic inference, and server `--auto-attach` are refused. A fresh manual
80	session requires the fresh exact PID/HWND/nonce challenge via

202	  -> Windows Graphics Capture for the selected window, RGBA frame

317	## Known limits
318	
319	- Pixel checks reject malformed, blank and tiny frames; they do not positively
320	  identify a real table. Wrong title calibration and correlated model errors remain
321	  possible.
322	- The 8-second maximum frame age is independent of the tighter 5-second total
323	  deadline. Published leases use the shorter remaining limit, not a new lifetime
324	  from delivery. Consumers must honor invalidation, absolute expiry and EOF even
325	  when capture blocks.
326	- Persistently animated tiles (seat avatars, badges, glows) are excluded from
327	  change detection while they animate, so a state change inside such a tile is
328	  only picked up by the periodic forced refresh (5 s by default), not instantly.
329	  On a live six-max table real state changes arrive every few hundred
330	  milliseconds; an inference of several seconds rarely finds a quiet window.
331	- Strict continuity may suppress valid hands after missed frames or street changes.
332	  Multiway all-in and side-pot decisions remain suppressed; poker math is unchanged.
333	- Real image accuracy, end-to-end latency, DPI behavior, window occlusion, restart
334	  recovery and clean-account packaging require recorded physical evidence.
335	- Six-max capture support is not complete six-player strategy support. Preserve
336	  heads-up-only raising and multiway all-in/side-pot guards. Unknown cards,
337	  amounts, offered actions and history stay unavailable, not fabricated zeros.
338	- Laya server/dashboard support and the local fine-tuned checkpoint are absent
339	  from the historical release packaging. The source-free bundle is not a current
340	  Laya/dashboard installation; this phase makes no release/workflow changes.
341	- Lobby evaluation is thin: one eval-only image does not validate general lobby
342	  recognition or the configured lobby-size guard. Capture cursor compositing
343	  remains a limitation, and currency-glyph handling is untested.
344	- Weights remain local-only and nonredistributed. Template matching is an option
345	  for the user's decision, not an implemented or validated substitute for Laya.
346	- Root `lobby-screengrab.png` remains for the user to delete. The private eval-only
347	  copy and the reference PNGs/PDF are retained; the helper does not delete them.

===== README.md =====
# coinpoker-help

Local bug-bounty proof of concept for poker observation and decision support.
Native capture targets Windows 10 version 1903 or later. Structured JSON replay
and poker libraries also run on Linux.
The current helper has no mouse/keyboard input path, client-memory reader, or
client-network interception.

**Status:** engineering candidate, version `0.1.0`; Laya iteration-1 Gate F
**FAIL**, human verification **UNVERIFIED**, no validated live seated advice. A build,
synthetic evaluation or loaded model is not real-table acceptance. Physical
Windows, model, real-image and clean-account evidence is recorded in
[the Windows report](docs/WINDOWS_ACCEPTANCE_V1.md); unrun gates stay `UNRUN`.
Practice and cash use this same repo, representation and validation mechanism,
without a practice-only bypass. No real-money acceptance has been established.

## Start here

- [First manual seated diagnostic: launch, confirm, stop and checklist](docs/SEATED_DIAGNOSTIC.md)
- [Windows setup and local dashboard](docs/INSTALL_WINDOWS.md)
- [VLM compatibility and provenance](docs/VLM_COMPATIBILITY.md)
- [Live JSON-lines contract](docs/EVENTS_V2.md)
- [Visual evaluation contract](docs/VISUAL_EVALUATION_V2.md)
- [Model terms](MODEL_LICENSES.md), [security](SECURITY.md), [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)

## Current model and browser

The sole perception backend is Laya Vision. Reuse the already downloaded and
trained checkpoint `models/laya-vision/finetuned/20261009T190322Z-it1`, based on
`thaitea/laya-vision@f2fe3c12cb6d04c59d8a190250bf3fb40fc828dc` and recorded in
`scripts/laya-pins.json`. No redownload, retraining or new dump is needed for
this dashboard phase. A fresh install lacks this user's local fine-tuned weights.

The canonical browser address is **`http://127.0.0.1:18090/`**. Model metadata
is at `/v1/models` under alias `coinpoker-laya-vision`; typed Laya requests use
`/v1/laya/predict` on the same listener. Gemma, ports `18080`/`8080`,
chat-completions and remote VLM opt-in are retired product instructions, not
alternate endpoints or fallbacks.

The browser has exactly two views, **Monitor** and **Reference** in a compact
landscape companion. Monitor shows source/role/freshness, independent readings,
six physical seats and a separate recorder status; history and diagnostics are
collapsible. A genuine current full native observation and matching decision can
display **EXPERIMENTAL** analysis with `quality_approved:false`; partial readouts
cannot supply it. The pinned model's R17 and untrained hero/control limitations
remain, and no live seated capability or quality certification is claimed.
Reference uses a searchable topic list and selected content, with the existing
bundled education and citations unchanged.
It makes no runtime content requests and does not copy the root charts.

Open `http://127.0.0.1:18090/` beside the selected table. **Stop capture** requests
termination of the current source session through the service-bound local
`POST /api/capture/stop`; it does not need a loaded model. There are currently no
HTTP start/mark, seating or betting controls. For development startup, choose
one mode below, not two concurrent servers; inspect the existing 18090 listener
before starting anything. Reuse an already running service.

```powershell
# Dashboard-only startup without loading a model or using the GPU.
pwsh -File scripts/start-vlm.ps1 -DashboardOnly
```

```powershell
# Normal startup is also dashboard-only. No automatic model load or attachment.
pwsh -File scripts/start-vlm.ps1
```

The role display follows explicit current-source evidence: **Observing**,
**Seated** ("Waiting for your turn"), **Your turn**, or **Reading uncertain**.
Observing call cost/pot odds belong to the labelled acting seat, never a fictitious
"your call". Sitting down changes the role, not the stream or accumulated history.
Unknown readings stay unknown; a missing feed is one compact message, not a grid
of unavailable fields. Expiry, heartbeat loss, hidden/resumed tabs and disconnects
clear current readings without renewing their leases. Runtime/lease/ledger details
and synthetic fixtures stay behind the scenes, not in extra app views.

Normal startup no longer follows a saved selector. `-LiveConfig`, a supplied
`-PracticeConfig` without explicit automatic inference, and server `--auto-attach` are refused. A fresh manual
session requires the fresh exact PID/HWND/nonce challenge via
`scripts/laya_capture.py`, with identity rechecked within 30 seconds. No seating
assertion is required; replacement requires new source confirmation. Default first-session
limits are **600 seconds or 1,200 saved frames**, whichever comes first. Model
loading requires separately approved `-EnableInference`; it never starts capture.
See the [manual runbook](docs/SEATED_DIAGNOSTIC.md) for commands and draft markers.

For explicitly approved observation of one confirmed table window until it closes,
use the sustained mode after verifying/stopping only the owned existing service:

```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/start-vlm.ps1 -EnableInference -AutomaticInference -ContinuousObservation
```

All three flags are required. This reuses the confirmed private source profile;
it never follows a replacement or changes the poker client. Evidence recording
still stops at 600 seconds, 1,200 saved frames, or 1 GiB, but newly acquired live
frames continue through bounded in-memory transport. Monitor labels that distinction
and puts stop reasons in its main view. Field confidence floors and five-second
reading leases are unchanged; unknown role/activity does not hide independent
admitted numeric fields. Page refresh starts nothing. Source/visibility/owner/model
failure or an explicit stop ends observation without automatic resume. This mode
does not run experimental p6/p7 diagnostics, strategy, or timer recognition.
Synthetic sustained tests are not real-window recognition acceptance.

Some client windows draw the CoinPoker logo and `NLH` number inside their frame
but expose only `CoinPoker` as the OS title. A confirmed private selector can
use that exact OS title. This is **not** an automatic lobby fallback: it requires
explicit user confirmation and still fails on multiple visible matches. Source
identity, current dimensions and perception-quality gates stay independent;
transition/loading/lobby captures are not positive table labels.

Current profile metadata uses `user_scope:"six-max-table"`, not a practice/cash
mode restriction. Legacy `practice-six-max` profiles load with the identical
exact selector, without rewriting the source file or broadening its matches.
`.local/practice-table.json` and `-PracticeConfig` remain compatibility names;
neither names nor window titles prove the actual game mode or layout.

The native recorder saves only private PNGs and a durable SHA-256 manifest under
`.local/captures/<UTC>-practice/`. The historical generic recorder defaults were
7,200 frames, 1 GiB and 500 ms; the new bounded manual entry point overrides the
frame limit to 1,200 and adds the independent 600-second stop.
Caps or I/O failures preserve the prefix and stop new recording without deleting
evidence. The manual session never rearms or follows a replacement. No images, paths or window titles are
served to the browser. Real counters are separate from capture-health counters.
The confirmed real-window B check recorded 900x686 frames, followed the
replacement table and captured its 800x613-to-879x670 resize. SHA-256 audits passed
for 322 original, 9 transition and 118 replacement-prefix frames; old evidence
remains in separate private sessions. This establishes capture and recording,
**not usable recognition**: no observations passed the fitted gate, so Monitor
shows `Reading uncertain`. No timed C/seated session or full reading-to-Monitor
latency acceptance has occurred. Seated controls/hero amounts and calculated metrics
require the later genuine-data/quality checkpoints; a null metric is not zero.
Private session history uses opaque IDs, not player names or cross-session guesses.

Checkpoint A validation: 402 Rust tests passed (one ignored), 79 Python tests
passed, and 47 desktop/400px browser checks passed with no JavaScript errors or
mutation/external requests. Doctor has ten passes and discovery blocked (exit 1).
These tests use synthetic role observations, not real seated recognition or
capture-to-Monitor latency acceptance. Receipts remain private under `.local/`.

Checkpoint B software verification: 425 Rust passes (one ignored), 161 Python
passes, successful pinned-artifact verification, and refreshed desktop/400px UI
checks without JavaScript errors. The existing launcher replaced the old service
only after verifying it stopped; one it1 model remains on 18090. Capture and
manifest checks now pass; source-current poker readings remain unaccepted.
The old it1 fitted acceptance floors are now enforced independently from
temperature calibration; board `1.0` is never lowered or rounded into acceptance.

The baseline receipt stays failed: board threshold `1.0` gave **0/330 confident
board units** on the 66 agent-reviewed frames, despite raw accuracy
`307/330 = 93.03%`. Warm full-battery p95 was **3027.3 ms**, failing the original
`<2000 ms` Gate F target. The prospective `<5000 ms` warm capture-to-display p95
and hard 5000 ms full end-to-end deadline do not retroactively pass that run;
the old benchmark was not seated or capture-to-browser timing. Temperature
calibration is not capability approval; source/vendor `calibrated:false` remains.
Positive real UI data and approved human-held-out calibration/evaluation are
required before seated advice.

**Perception repair stage2 (2026-10-10):** approved implementation is verified
offline, not live-accepted. Partial read-only fields are separate from strict
GameState/R17. Independent pot/sixstacks, source-region witnesses/originalexpiry,
gated per-seat wagers and occupancy/status/badge/button/blind/acting paths are
wired. New capabilities require their own pinned crop/floor/evidence/human-held-out
proof; defaults remainuntrained/unknown. No suggestions/metrics or qualitypromotion.
Monitor/Reference remain the onlyviews; stack and wager are distinct, and
unsupported contributions remain unknown in secondary diagnostics.

Workspace506pass/1realcaptureignored, offlinePython/Node207pass, strictclippy pass.
Saved-answer regression preserves pot+3/5/5stackcandidates withstrictnull, not live
accuracy/latencyproof. Private receipts andNEWunlabeled72framev2 index staylocal.
No helper/modelreload, GPUtraining, new observing/capture or gameinput occurred.
Realquality, hand/convention evidence, browser/mobile and warmtotalp95 are pending
separate gates; GateF FAIL/humanUNVERIFIED/suggestionsOFF unchanged.

Historical stage1 diagnosis: native observing assembly previously skipped trained stack
passes, discards players and lacks wagers/badges/dealer/acting-seat extraction.
This is a recognition/integration failure, not successful tracking. Saved-frame
replay isolated failed unseated/phase questions and zero board admission at the
unchanged 1.0 floor; independent pot/stack glyphs often meet their own old floors.
A confident wrong phase also shows why semantic checks remain necessary. These
historical diagnostic candidates are not Monitor reads or human acceptance.

Proposed repair separates calibrated source-leased **partial read-only
observations** from fully validated actionable `GameState`, with explicit six
physical slots, distinct stacks/wagers/street contributions, hand positions and
betting gaps. R17 remains; partial data cannot enable experimental decisions. No warm total capture-to-Monitor
latency/live recognition gate has passed. [Vision section 7](docs/LAYA_VISION_PHASE_A.md)
records outcomes and later gates; private receipts and a pending 72-frame human
checklist remain local.

`screenshot-1.png`, `screenshot-2.png` and `poker-info-sheet.pdf` are odds,
six-handed raise-first-in and rules references, respectively. They remain
historical deterministic calculation material, not the source of the new
researched Reference or positive hero-button/seated-card UI examples.
Reference displays are not live recommendations.

## Architecture

```text
Windows process and window metadata (exe name, PID, HWND)
  -> unique source-specific confirmed game-window selection, explicit ambiguity
  -> Windows Graphics Capture for the selected window, RGBA frame
  -> cumulative and local pixel change checks, persistently animated tiles
     suppressed (seat avatars, badges, glows), stability gate
  -> one inference worker and one replaceable latest frame
  -> generation, epoch, window identity and capture-age checks
  -> strict screen classification and complete poker-state validation
  -> two matching fresh observations and hand transition guards
  -> Monte Carlo equity and legal decision pipeline
  -> JSON-lines status, leased decision, clear, or discarded event
```

The native capture loop continues during a blocking local Laya
request. A changed or lost window, ambiguous selection, stale frame, or expired
lease clears active advice. Configured source identity and strict recognition,
quality and action validation are required before a visual recommendation. Repeated
model agreement is not independent proof of correct recognition; the held-out
real-image gate remains necessary.

The workspace crates are `ingest` (capture and vision), `core-engine` (poker math),
`ghost-layer` (unwired timing primitives), `opponent-model`, `ui` (unwired native
desktop panel), and `bin` (CLI, replay, diagnostics and evaluation). The current
browser is a local observation dashboard with no input execution layer. Observed
controls, history, calculated metrics and eventual recommendations stay separate;
legacy table events and raw model answers are not trusted current hero actions.

## CLI

From a source checkout, run these in PowerShell after following the install guide:

```powershell
cargo run --release --locked --bin coinpoker -- --help
cargo run --release --locked --bin coinpoker -- --stdin
cargo run --release --locked --bin coinpoker -- --list-windows
cargo run --release --locked --bin coinpoker -- --doctor
cargo run --release --locked --bin coinpoker -- --evaluate fixtures/synthetic/manifest.json
```

The historical source-free candidate archive supports bundled CLI/replay checks:

```powershell
& .\coinpoker.exe --help
& .\coinpoker.exe --stdin
& .\coinpoker.exe --list-windows
& .\coinpoker.exe --doctor
& .\coinpoker.exe --evaluate fixtures/synthetic/manifest.json
```

The real client executable and title conventions must come from `--list-windows` on
the actual installed client. The listing reads public metadata and may contain
personal window titles. It captures no pixels. The following low-level selector
example is internal calibration/diagnostic tooling, not a Monitor connect step:

```powershell
$env:COINPOKER_EXE_NAME = '<observed executable name>'
$env:COINPOKER_WINDOW_TITLE = '<observed table-only title fragment>'
$env:COINPOKER_LOBBY_TITLE = '<observed lobby title fragment>'
cargo run --release --locked --bin coinpoker
```

This is not the dashboard-only first-phase startup. With the current helper,
seating and play are manual; capture alone does not establish analysis eligibility.
The old candidate binary invocation is:

```powershell
& .\coinpoker.exe
```

CLI values override nonempty environment values, which override defaults. Invalid
values fail instead of being clamped. `--help` lists all timing and pixel bounds.

| CLI | Environment | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--exe-name` | `COINPOKER_EXE_NAME` | Exact calibrated executable basename, required for live discovery |
| `--pid` | `COINPOKER_PID` | Optional process pin; remove it for restart recovery |
| `--window-hwnd` | `COINPOKER_WINDOW_HWND` | Optional hexadecimal HWND pin; remove it for replacement-window recovery |
| `--table-title` | `COINPOKER_WINDOW_TITLE` | Calibrated table-only substring, required for advice |
| `--lobby-title` | `COINPOKER_LOBBY_TITLE` | Lobby veto that takes precedence over a table hint |
| `--lobby-size` | `COINPOKER_LOBBY_SIZE` | Observed lobby `WIDTHxHEIGHT`. The same title at another size is the table |
| `--vlm-endpoint` | `COINPOKER_VLM_ENDPOINT` | Sole local target: `http://127.0.0.1:18090/v1/laya/predict` |
| `--vlm-model` | `COINPOKER_VLM_MODEL` | Sole pinned alias: `coinpoker-laya-vision`; verify through `/v1/models` |
| `--timeout-secs` | `COINPOKER_VLM_TIMEOUT_SECS` | Per-request timeout, default 5 seconds; not a fresh budget for every phase |
| `--decision-budget-ms` | `COINPOKER_DECISION_BUDGET_MS` | Total source-capture deadline, default 5000 ms, bounds 500..5000; reserves 300 ms for publication/poll/render |
| `--retry-ms` | `COINPOKER_RETRY_MS` | Default 2000 ms; bounded recovery delay |

Equal-ranked windows produce an ambiguity state. A PID or HWND pin is a deliberate
restriction and will wait if its target disappears. Title strings and public process
metadata are user calibration, not cryptographic proof that a window is a table.

## Privacy and model provenance

Explicit native capture requests the selected window through Windows Graphics
Capture. The pixel boundary still needs physical evidence. Laya receives local
PNG region requests; browser snapshots/history must not expose captures, raw
model replies, backend bodies or player names. The service binds loopback only;
there is no supported remote opt-in. Keep new capture pixels under
`.local/captures/` and diagnostics private. Local logs, swap and crash dumps need
separate review; private answer logs are diagnostics, never advice inputs.

`download-model.ps1 -Verify` verifies existing Laya files against
`scripts/laya-pins.json`. Repository source is MIT; the pinned Laya fork and
upstream SmolVLM backbone are Apache-2.0, but Laya weights and the local derivative are
CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 and are not redistributed. See [model terms](MODEL_LICENSES.md)
and [compatibility evidence](docs/VLM_COMPATIBILITY.md). The orphaned
`scripts/vlm-pins.json` is historical only.

## Structured replay

`--stdin` consumes one complete `GameState` per line and retains its existing bare
decision and clear records. It does not need capture or model setup. Invalid input
clears an active recommendation once; later valid input may recover.

```json
{"game_phase":"flop","hero_cards":[{"rank":"A","suit":"spades"},{"rank":"K","suit":"hearts"}],"board":[{"rank":"A","suit":"diamonds"},{"rank":"7","suit":"clubs"},{"rank":"2","suit":"spades"}],"pot_size":1000,"to_call":500,"hero_chips":5000,"min_raise_to":1500,"max_raise_to":5000,"players":[{"name":"Hero","chips":5000,"last_action":"check","bet_amount":0},{"name":"Villain","chips":4500,"last_action":"bet","bet_amount":500}],"action_required":true,"available_actions":["fold","call","raise"]}
```

## Known limits

- Pixel checks reject malformed, blank and tiny frames; they do not positively
  identify a real table. Wrong title calibration and correlated model errors remain
  possible.
- The 8-second maximum frame age is independent of the tighter 5-second total
  deadline. Published leases use the shorter remaining limit, not a new lifetime
  from delivery. Consumers must honor invalidation, absolute expiry and EOF even
  when capture blocks.
- Persistently animated tiles (seat avatars, badges, glows) are excluded from
  change detection while they animate, so a state change inside such a tile is
  only picked up by the periodic forced refresh (5 s by default), not instantly.
  On a live six-max table real state changes arrive every few hundred
  milliseconds; an inference of several seconds rarely finds a quiet window.
- Strict continuity may suppress valid hands after missed frames or street changes.

entries.description: Semantic search. Returns verbatim drawer content with similarity scores. IMPORTANT: 'query' must contain ONLY search keywords. Use 'context' for background. Results with cosine distance > max_distance are filtered out.

query.description: Short search query ONLY — keywords or a question. Max 250 chars.

source_file.description: Filter to one exact source_file (optional). Matches the full stored path exactly (leading/trailing whitespace trimmed); no glob or basename matching. Pass the value from a result's 'source_path' field; the displayed 'source_file' is only a basename.

since.description: Only drawers filed on/after this ISO date or datetime (inclusive), e.g. '2026-04-01' or '2026-04-01T09:30:00'. Compares the drawer's created_at (filed_at) wall-clock; drawers without a filed_at are excluded while set.

before.description: Only drawers filed strictly before this ISO date or datetime (exclusive). Same comparison rules as 'since'.

max_distance.description: Max cosine distance threshold (0=identical, 2=opposite). Results further than this are dropped. Lower = stricter. Default 1.5. Set to 0 to disable.

candidate_strategy.description: Candidate source strategy. 'vector' preserves default semantic search; 'union' also merges backend BM25 lexical candidates before reranking.

cli_compatible.description: Preserve standalone CLI candidate selection, ranking, and output. Used by the CLI Hub forwarder.

context.description: Background context for the search (optional). NOT used for embedding — only for future re-ranking.
