Limitations and Source Use
Hand Rankings and Ties

Standard high-hand Hold'em; best five cards, not starting-hand strength.

At showdown, compare the best five-card hand available from seven cards. Hold'em permits zero, one, or two hole cards. First compare the hand category, then the ranks that define it; never use a sixth or seventh card to break a tie.

An ace is high except in A-2-3-4-5, a five-high straight (the wheel). T-J-Q-K-A is ace-high. Q-K-A-2-3 does not wrap into a straight. The same ace-low rule applies to straight flushes.
Kickers count only within the best five cards. With the same pair, compare the three remaining cards from highest to lowest; stop at the first difference.
Suits do not rank above one another. Identical best five-card ranks split the eligible pot, including when the board plays for everyone; house rules allocate any odd chip.
Strongest to weakest; a royal flush is the highest straight flush
Order	Hand	Definition and comparison
1	Royal flush	A-K-Q-J-T of one suit; tied royals share the pot.
2	Straight flush	Five sequential ranks of one suit; compare the top rank.
3	Four of a kind	Four equal ranks; compare quads, then the remaining kicker.
4	Full house	Three equal ranks plus a pair; compare trips first, then the pair.
5	Flush	Five of one suit; compare all five ranks from highest to lowest.
6	Straight	Five sequential ranks; compare only the top rank (wheel = five).
7	Three of a kind	Three equal ranks; compare trips, then the two kickers in order.
8	Two pair	Compare the higher pair, then the lower pair, then the kicker.
9	One pair	Compare the pair, then the three kickers in order.
10	High card	No higher category; compare all five ranks in descending order.

# Live observations of the Monitor at http://127.0.0.1:18090/ (2026-10-15)

Server: `pwsh -File scripts/start-vlm.ps1 -DashboardOnly` (dashboard-only, no model, no capture). Nothing else was listening on 18090 before launch.
Server ready line: `{"event": "ready", "host": "127.0.0.1", "port": 18090, "alias": "coinpoker-laya-vision", "dashboard": true, "advice_ready": false}`

## HTTP surface observed with curl
- `GET /` 200 text/html 15307 bytes. Headers: `Cache-Control: no-store`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, CSP `default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'none'`. HTTP/1.0, `Connection: close` on every response (new TCP connection per 250 ms poll).
- `GET /api/state` 200 JSON (saved at `api-state.json` beside this file). Dashboard-only state: `source:"idle"`, `model_state:"disabled"`, `quality_gate:"failed"`, `inference_enabled:false`, `capture.state:"idle"`, `observation:null`, `partial_observation:null`, `capture_session` present with the LAST sustained session from disk (status stopped, stop_reason operator-stop, evidence 10:00/10:00, 862/1200 frames, 673,427,602 bytes).
- `GET /v1/models` -> `{"error":"model-not-ready"}` (expected in dashboard-only mode).
- `GET /api/reference` 200 JSON 20165 bytes (but the page never fetches it; app.js bundles LOCAL_REFERENCE inline and `loadReference()` reads that constant).
- `GET /nope` 404 JSON `{"error":"not-found"}`; `GET /../README.md` (path as-is) 404.
- `Host: evil.example` -> 403. `POST /api/capture/stop` with `Origin: https://evil.example` -> 403; same-origin with junk ids -> 400.

## Rendered page, clean load, 800x600 pane (screenshots)
- Desktop clean load: `tool-results/REDACTED.jpg`
- Diagnostics panel expanded: `tool-results/REDACTED.jpg`
- Diagnostics scrolled: `tool-results/REDACTED.jpg`
- 1280x800: `tool-results/REDACTED.jpg`
- Mobile 375x812 top: `tool-results/REDACTED.jpg`
- Mobile 375x812 scrolled: `tool-results/REDACTED.jpg`

(All under `C:\Users\cld-main\.claude\projects\C--Users-cld-main-Desktop-github-projects-coinpoker-help\9a033a56-779b-418e-881d-7f600baf0875\`.)

Visible text on a clean load: source strip "Session stopped / Role unknown / No current capture"; buttons "Start monitor" and "Stop monitor" both disabled with "Manual start not configured."; sr-only empty message "Session stopped. Readings cleared."; Table panel with "Experimental" badge, "Occupancy uncertain", six seat cards each "Seat N / Seat status pending / <location> / Stack - / Wager -" with reasons "Insufficient context" (stack) and "Untrained" (wager); center "UPPER POT -" with "Insufficient context"; five dashed board slots labelled Flop/Turn/River with "Unknown / Insufficient context"; collapsed "Diagnostics and manual test" details; footer "Local diagnostic companion / No automated poker actions".

Diagnostics expanded shows: "No current reading", "Evidence recording ended / last received / duration-limit", "Inference OFF / session stopped", lifecycle box "Session stopped: operator-stop. Current and last-read amounts cleared." with the relaunch command `scripts/start-vlm.ps1 -EnableInference -AutomaticInference -ContinuousObservation`, Model "Service inference OFF; model disabled / idle; quality failed", Source ages "Capture unknown / reading unavailable / observation 11:58", Recorder budget "Evidence 10:00 / 10:00; 862 / 1,200 frames; 673,427,602 / 1,073,741,824 bytes", Loss/gaps "0 capture failures / 34 gaps; 34 estimated missed samples; max 1,397 ms", Opportunities "0 / 20 draft markers; deficit 20", and a 14-row field diagnostics grid (Untrained / Insufficient context).

## Verified behaviours / defects seen live
1. STICKY "Stale" LABELS AFTER RECONNECT (confirmed by code + live): when the page was opened before the server was listening, the first poll failed -> `disconnected()` -> `clearObservation("stale")` sets `clearReason="stale"`. After the server came up and `/api/state` returned a snapshot with no observation, `admitObservation` -> `fencedObservation(null)` -> `clearObservation()` keeps the default `reason = clearReason` ("stale"). Result: every field reason read "Stale" (pot, board, all six stacks) and the board said "Unknown / Stale" although nothing was ever read. A clean reload with the server already up shows "Insufficient context" instead. `clearReason` is only reset to "insufficient-context" inside a successful `admitObservation`. See app.js `reasonFor()` (~line 505), `clearObservation()` (~2359), `disconnected()` (~2372), `admitObservation()` (~2423).
2. HISTORICAL SESSION PRESENTED AS CURRENT STATE: a brand-new dashboard-only server reports the last on-disk sustained session (from 2026-10-14) as `capture_session` status "stopped"; the Monitor's primary status reads "Session stopped" and the empty-state says "Session stopped. Readings cleared." with no date/time or "previous session" qualifier. A user cannot tell this is yesterday's receipt rather than something that just stopped.
3. MOBILE OVERLAP (375px): the seat freshness indicator (absolutely positioned 7px circle at right:9px/top:9px in `.spatial-seats .seat-freshness`) overlaps the last glyph of "Seat status pending" in every seat card. The seat-identity span uses `white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis` but the button grid gives it the full width, so the text runs under the dot.
4. Both "Start monitor" and "Stop monitor" render as disabled buttons in dashboard-only mode with the status "Manual start not configured." No affordance explains how to configure it from the page (the relaunch command appears only inside the collapsed Diagnostics panel).
5. Console: one `net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` from before the server started; no JavaScript errors after a clean load. Polling is `/api/state` every 250 ms with `cache: no-store`, HTTP/1.0 `Connection: close` (a fresh TCP connection four times a second).
6. A 100 ms `setInterval(refreshClocks)` re-renders the whole observation (`renderObservation`) ten times a second even when idle (`refreshClocks` returns early only when disconnected/hidden).
7. The visible "view-label" span (`#view-label`) is `display:none` in CSS; the only view description is the tab itself.
8. `#analysis-status` badge "Analysis unavailable" sits in the masthead at all times; on mobile it wraps to its own line under the brand.

Files to read (read them fully; follow imports where needed): ${r.files} Questions you must answer with path:line evidence: ${r.questions} Also: measure lines of code per file (wc -l), classify each component's maturity honestly (stub / scaffold / partial / working / hardened / unwired / historical), list dead or unwired code, summarise test coverage and whether it exercises real inputs or synthetic ones, list open questions you could not resolve from code, and estimate this subsystem's percent progress toward what the README/HANDOFF say it must do, with rationale. Aim for depth over breadth: 8-20 components, 5-12 weaknesses with severities, 3-8 strengths.` } function lensPrompt(l) { return `${COMMON} YOUR TASK: you are a senior front-end expert reviewing the Monitor web UI through the lens "${l.title}". Primary sources: scripts/dashboard/index.html (153 lines), scripts/dashboard/app.js (2,858 lines; the bundled reference JSON occupies lines 4-359 and the state constants start at line 362), scripts/dashboard/styles.css (282 lines), scripts/dashboard/reference.json; server side scripts/laya-server.py (routes near lines 880-1000) and scripts/laya_dashboard.py (DashboardState DTO); tests scripts/tests/test_companion_ui.py, test_monitor_controls_ui.py, test_laya_numeric_ui.py, test_laya_visual_ui.py; docs README.md (section "Current model and browser"), HANDOFF.md, docs/EVENTS_V2.md, SECURITY.md. Read ${SCRATCH}/live-observations.md first and look at the screenshots it lists (Read the JPG paths). The live dashboard-only server at http://127.0.0.1:18090/ may be probed with read-only GETs only. Focus: ${l.focus} Return up to 12 findings ranked by severity, each with a stable id prefixed "${l.key}-", concrete path:line or screenshot evidence, operator impact, a specific recommendation and an effort estimate; list genuine strengths; and give a 1-10 score for this lens with rationale. Severity guide: critical = misleads the operator about reading validity or breaks the page; high = materially degrades use or maintainability; medium = should fix before wider use; low = polish; nit = taste.` } function uiVerifyPrompt(kind, lens, result) { return `${COMMON} YOUR TASK: you are an independent skeptic ("${kind.key}") verifying findings produced by another reviewer for the lens "${lens.title}". ${kind.instruction} Sources: scripts/dashboard/{index.html, app.js, styles.css}, scripts/laya-server.py, scripts/laya_dashboard.py, scripts/tests/test_companion_ui.py, ${SCRATCH}/live-observations.md and its screenshots, ${SCRATCH}/api-state.json. Default to upheld=false when you cannot confirm a finding. For each finding return upheld, an adjusted severity, and a one-to-three sentence note citing the decisive evidence. FINDINGS TO VERIFY (JSON): ${JSON.stringify(result.findings, null, 1)}` } function assessPrompt(d, maps, frontend) { const uiSummary = frontend.filter(Boolean).map(l => ({ lens: l.lens, score: l.score, upheld: l.findings.filter(f => f.verdict === 'upheld').map(f => ({ id: f.id, title: f.title, severity: f.severity })), refuted: l.findings.filter(f => f.verdict !== 'upheld').map(f => f.id) })) return `${COMMON} YOUR TASK: you are a principal engineer assessing the dimension "${d.title}". Guidance: ${d.hint} You have the structured maps produced by ten subsystem readers (JSON below) and a summary of the verified frontend review. Read any repository file you need to confirm or extend a point; do not take a map's statement on faith if it decides your grade. Produce: a letter grade and 0-100 score; a six-to-twelve sentence summary; 5-10 falsifiable claims with path:line evidence and your confidence (these will be adversarially checked, so only claim what you can point to); and 4-10 prioritized recommendations (P0 = blocks the stated goal, P1 = should precede the next live run, P2 = next sprint, P3 = later) with effort. SUBSYSTEM MAPS: ${JSON.stringify(maps, null, 1)} VERIFIED FRONTEND REVIEW SUMMARY: ${JSON.stringify(uiSummary, null, 1)}` } function claimVerifyPrompt(kind, assessment) { return `${COMMON} YOUR TASK: you are an independent skeptic ("${kind.key}") checking the factual claims of an assessment titled "${assessment.dimension}". ${kind.instruction} CLAIMS (JSON): ${JSON.stringify(assessment.claims, null, 1)}` } phase('Map') log('Mapping ten subsystems and reviewing the frontend through seven lenses in parallel') const mapsPromise = parallel(READERS.map(r => () => agent(readerPrompt(r), { label: `map:${r.key}`, phase: 'Map', schema: MAP_SCHEMA }))) const frontendPromise = pipeline( LENSES, l => agent(lensPrompt(l), { label: `ui:${l.key}`, phase: 'Frontend review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA }), (result, l) => { if (!result) return null if (!result.findings.length) return { ...result, findings: [] } return parallel(UI_VERIFIERS.map(kind => () => agent(uiVerifyPrompt(kind, l, result), { label: `verify:${l.key}:${kind.key}`, phase: 'Verify UI findings', schema: VERDICTS_SCHEMA }))) .then(votes => { const valid = votes.filter(Boolean) const findings = result.findings.map(f => { const vs = valid.map(v => v.verdicts.find(x => x.id === f.id)).filter(Boolean) const upheldCount = vs.filter(v => v.upheld).length const verdict = vs.length === 0 ? 'unverified' : upheldCount * 2 >= vs.length ? 'upheld' : 'refuted' const sevOrder = ['nit', 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'critical'] const sevs = vs.filter(v => v.upheld).map(v => sevOrder.indexOf(v.adjusted_severity)).filter(i => i >= 0).sort((a, b) => a - b) const adjusted = sevs.length ? sevOrder[sevs[Math.floor(sevs.length / 2)]] : f.severity return { ...f, original_severity: f.severity, severity: adjusted, verdict, votes: vs } }) log(`UI lens ${l.key}: ${findings.filter(f => f.verdict === 'upheld').length}/${findings.length} findings upheld`) return { ...result, findings } }) } ) const maps = (await mapsPromise).filter(Boolean) log(`Maps complete: ${maps.length}/${READERS.length} subsystems mapped`) const frontend = (await frontendPromise).filter(Boolean) log(`Frontend review complete: ${frontend.length}/${LENSES.length} lenses`) phase('Assess') const assessments = (await pipeline( DIMENSIONS, d => agent(assessPrompt(d, maps, frontend), { label: `assess:${d.key}`, phase: 'Assess', schema: ASSESS_SCHEMA }), (a, d) => { if (!a) return null return parallel(CLAIM_VERIFIERS.map(kind => () => agent(claimVerifyPrompt(kind, a), { label: `claims:${d.key}:${kind.key}`, phase: 'Verify claims', schema: CLAIM_VERDICTS_SCHEMA }))) .then(votes => { const valid = votes.filter(Boolean) const claims = a.claims.map(c => { const vs = valid.map(v => v.verdicts.find(x => x.id === c.id)).filter(Boolean) const refuted = vs.some(v => v.refuted && v.confidence >= 0.6) return { ...c, status: vs.length === 0 ? 'unverified' : refuted ? 'refuted' : 'upheld', votes: vs } }) log(`Assessment ${d.key}: ${claims.filter(c => c.status === 'upheld').length}/${claims.length} claims upheld`) return { ...a, claims } }) } )).filter(Boolean) phase('Critique') const criticInput = { maps: maps.map(m => ({ subsystem: m.subsystem, summary: m.summary, progress: m.progress, weaknesses: m.weaknesses.map(w => `${w.severity}: ${w.title}`), open_questions: m.open_questions })), frontend: frontend.map(l => ({ lens: l.lens, score: l.score, upheld: l.findings.filter(f => f.verdict === 'upheld').map(f => `${f.severity}: ${f.title}`) })), assessments: assessments.map(a => ({ dimension: a.dimension, grade: a.grade, score: a.score, summary: a.summary, refuted_claims: a.claims.filter(c => c.status === 'refuted').map(c => c.claim), recommendations: a.recommendations.map(r => `${r.priority}: ${r.title}`) })), } const critic = await agent(`${COMMON} YOUR TASK: you are the completeness critic. The user asked for "a full and complete recursive analysis of the progress of this repo" and "an expert appraisal of the frontend at 127.0.0.1:18090". Review the condensed results below and answer: what is missing? Which directory, file, flow, claim or question did nobody examine or verify? Which refuted claims leave a hole? Is any important part of the tree (every top-level directory: .cargo .github .kilo .local bin crates dist docs fixtures graphify-out models scripts tests target) unaccounted for? Note: there is a top-level directory named tests/ (created 2026-10-14) that no reader was assigned; check what it contains. Return up to 6 gaps, each with a complete self-contained task brief an agent can execute read-only in under 15 minutes, plus a short overall assessment of the audit's coverage. CONDENSED RESULTS: ${JSON.stringify(criticInput, null, 1)}`, { label: 'critic', phase: 'Critique', schema: CRITIC_SCHEMA }) let gapFills = [] if (critic && critic.gaps.length) { log(`Critic found ${critic.gaps.length} gaps; filling them`) gapFills = (await parallel(critic.gaps.slice(0, 6).map((g, i) => () => agent(`${COMMON} YOUR TASK (gap fill ${i + 1}: ${g.title}): ${g.task_prompt} Return a concise, evidence-cited answer (path:line) of at most 600 words, as plain text.`, { label: `gap:${i + 1}`, phase: 'Critique' }).then(text => ({ title: g.title, why: g.why_it_matters, answer: text }))))).filter(Boolean) } phase('Synthesize') const report = await agent(`${COMMON} YOUR TASK: you are the lead author. Write the final report in GitHub-flavoured Markdown from the verified material below. Use only upheld findings and upheld claims as facts; you may mention refuted items briefly as "considered and rejected" where instructive. Every factual statement about code needs a path:line or receipt path. Write for the repository owner (an experienced engineer who runs the project with AI coding sessions) and be direct, specific and fair. Structure (use these headings): 1. Executive summary (10-15 sentences: what the project is, where it stands today, the single biggest finding on each of frontend and repo progress, the headline verdict). 2. Scorecard: a table of the seven frontend lenses (score /10) and the seven repo dimensions (grade and /100), plus an overall frontend score and overall progress percent with one-line rationale each. 3. Part A: Frontend appraisal of the Monitor at 127.0.0.1:18090: A.1 what the page does and how it is built; A.2 strengths; A.3 findings grouped by severity (critical, high, medium, low), each with evidence, impact and recommendation; A.4 a prioritized fix list (quick wins first); A.5 a realistic refactor shape if warranted. 4. Part B: Recursive repository analysis: B.1 the tree, subsystem by subsystem (every top-level directory and crate/script group) with maturity and percent progress; B.2 the data/control flow from capture to browser with where it is proven vs unproven; B.3 timeline of the five weeks of work and where effort went; B.4 verification integrity (tests, CI, evidence, claim accuracy); B.5 security, privacy and licensing; B.6 process and hygiene; B.7 risk register (table). 5. Part C: Progress verdict: percent complete vs the HANDOFF Definition of Done and vs the original README goal, what is demonstrated vs asserted, the exact blockers, and the next three milestones with exit criteria. 6. Part D: Prioritized roadmap (P0 / P1 / P2 / P3) merging frontend and repo recommendations, each with effort. 7. Appendix: method (agents, verification), evidence index (logs, receipts, screenshots), and the list of refuted findings/claims with one-line reasons. Length: 5,000-8,000 words. Tables where they help. No em dashes. Return only the Markdown. VERIFIED MATERIAL (JSON): ${JSON.stringify({ maps, frontend, assessments, critic: critic ? critic.overall_assessment : null, gapFills, liveObservationsPath: SCRATCH + '/live-observations.md' }, null, 1)}`, { label: 'synthesize', phase: 'Synthesize' }) return { report, maps, frontend, assessments, critic, gapFills }

# DIGEST: assessments

## Architecture and code quality of the hybrid Rust/Python system  grade C+ (62/100)
The hybrid split is sound in principle and clean at the manifest level: the five library crates declare no dependencies on each other and are wired only by `bin`, the Windows-only surface is confined to one `cfg(target_os)` module, and Python owns exactly what Rust should not (torch model serving, dashboard projection, process supervision, CPU recognition). The seams that matter for safety are engineered carefully at every layer: loopback-only transport, fail-closed DTO validation, schema-2 JSONL records whose leases can only shorten, and a 256 KiB publication cap; and the uncommitted refactor is a faithful code-motion step in the right direction (manual_inference.rs 3,504 to 900 lines, live.rs 2,189 to 913, laya-server.py 1,632 to 1,259, Python geometry constants now derived from regions.json). The dominant structural defect is that contracts are carried by repetition rather than by a shared source: the partial-observation field allowlist, the pinned acceptance floors, the DRAFT experimental crop bounds and the readout-batch convention each exist in two to five hand-copied places across Rust, Python and JavaScript, and no test exercises a Rust-built request against the Python validator, so drift passes both suites and fails only live. Geometry is unified only for the twelve trained regions; the actions, context, showdown and numeric lanes keep four incompatible reference systems with different title-bar handling and duplicated helper functions. Roughly 60% of library-crate code is inert on the live path (outs/ranges/table_rules, temporal/profile, the egui panel that the CLI refuses, the observer's action recording that only ever receives quality_approved:false), the core-engine module doc claims an integration that does not exist, and the lockfile carries two rand and two thiserror majors while CI compiles eframe for a feature nothing can launch. The remaining monoliths, a 2,858-line browser IIFE with 52 mutable module variables, a 2,411-line dashboard module with a 562-line ingest method and ~300 unreachable supervisor lines, and a server file with 19 unused imports, are exactly where every new lane must land. The test estate violates the evidence boundary by writing fixtures into .local/laya/train, and the CI definition cannot collect the Python suite on a clean clone because two modules import numpy/PIL at module level and one imports a gitignored file. Two perception pipelines now run side by side (Rust-assembled GPU partial_observation and Python CPU provisional lanes) with differently shaped DTOs merged only in the browser, so the hybrid is drifting toward two systems. The structure can carry the next phase only if the contract and geometry sources are unified first; otherwise each new field or region costs five coordinated edits in three languages.

## Security, privacy and licensing posture  grade C+ (72/100)
The loopback boundary itself is engineered well above proof-of-concept norms and I verified it in code rather than taking the maps on faith: the stdlib server requires exactly one Host in {127.0.0.1:port, localhost:port} and at most one matching Origin, discards POST bodies before answering 403, and stamps every hardened response with a default-src 'none' CSP, no-store, nosniff and no-referrer (scripts/laya-server.py:856-865, 884-895; scripts/laya_server_validation.py:37-38); the Rust client refuses any non-loopback host, credentials, query or fragment, never follows redirects or reads proxy env, bounds every body, and the product layer additionally pins port 18090 and /v1/laya/predict (crates/ingest/src/vlm.rs:146-196; bin/config.rs:311-318); no subprocess uses a shell, the Windows OCR helper takes bounded JSON over stdin, private paths are junction/symlink/reparse-guarded on both the Python and Rust sides, the browser receives an opaque 16-hex source_id rather than pid/hwnd/exe, feed failures are regex-redacted, and no secrets or .env files are tracked. Model licensing is handled correctly where it matters: weights are ignored at two levels, only models/.gitignore is tracked, the CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 derivative is documented as local-only in MODEL_LICENSES.md and scripts/laya-pins.json, pinned artifacts are size+SHA-256 verified, and every direct Rust dependency is MIT/Apache (rs_poker Apache-2.0). The posture loses its grade on fidelity and hygiene, not on the boundary. The shipped DTO contradicts the written policy in three places I traced end to end: OCR-recognised player screen names are published to the browser and rendered in seat cards, and are also persisted to .local/laya/events/<id>/context.jsonl; popup HWND/owner HWND/PID/window_class ride into /api/state via the profile capture when a tooltip is read and app.js explicitly accepts them; and GET /api/evidence/<sha256> serves original capture PNGs, while SECURITY.md, README, EVENTS_V2 and CONTRIBUTING all still promise no names, no native HWND/PID data and no images in browser output. Licensing of tracked content is weaker than the model story: a 16.5 MB PokerNews cheat-sheet PDF and two third-party reference-card PNGs are committed and pushed under an MIT LICENSE with no notice, while the design doc states they are untracked. A public test file hard-codes six real opponents' screen names next to private capture hashes, directly against CONTRIBUTING's rule. Evidence integrity is being eroded by the test suite itself, which writes thousands of synthetic sessions into the real .local evidence tree and imports a gitignored script. Residual loopback risks (SO_REUSEADDR on the listener, control_id published in /api/state, stdlib fallthrough for HEAD/OPTIONS, no dependency audit, version-only pip pins) are real but acknowledged by SECURITY.md's "unauthenticated listener" statement and do not block the stated live-readout goal.

The one solid pillar is toolchain and lock discipline: Rust 1.95.0 is pinned identically in rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.toml:21, both workflows and scripts/setup-windows.ps1, Cargo.lock is committed and consumed with --locked everywhere, scripts/validate.py mirrors ci.yml command for command, commit messages carry descriptive bodies, and the orchestrator verified fmt/check/clippy clean with 623 Rust and 814 Python tests green on the pinned host. Almost everything else about process is weak or inverted: commits are enormous and mixed (5889f14 touches 337 files and +559,612 lines; three more commits exceed +10,000), the history has zero merge commits or PRs, and the documented process in HANDOFF.md:121 and every .kilo plan is "keep everything uncommitted; the user commits", so a dirty worktree whose modified files depend on untracked sources (scripts/laya-server.py:53 imports the untracked laya_server_validation.py; three #[path] test modules are untracked) is the normal state. 93.5% of tracked bytes are a stale generated code graph (graphify-out: 45.75 MB, 247 files including two .tmp backup files, with GRAPH_REPORT.md:14 claiming it was built from 2f80e2fa) plus a 16.5 MB third-party PDF, both already pushed to origin, while the docs and plans still assert those files are "untracked by design". CI integrity cannot be trusted at HEAD: a tracked test module imports a gitignored .local file, two modules import numpy/PIL at module level while ci.yml installs bare Python 3.11 with no dependency step, the last documented green CI run is six commits old, and locally three different interpreters (3.11 in CI, 3.12.15 pinned, 3.14.3 used by validate.py) run the suite. Branch and dependency management are effectively abandoned: origin/main diverged at 0dfe5fa with seven overlay commits absent from the working line, local main points at a third commit, nine Dependabot branches sit ten commits behind with two targeting crates no longer in Cargo.lock, and the release workflow still ships the orphaned Gemma manifest while omitting every Laya file the shipped scripts actually read. The Rust and Python test suites write thousands of synthetic session directories into the private evidence tree (2,213 entries under .local/laya/train/*-inference-20261012/native, 114 added by today's run) beside real receipts, contradicting HANDOFF's own rule to keep synthetic and live evidence separate. Line-ending policy is incomplete (system core.autocrlf=true with .gitattributes covering only ps1/py/pdf), producing CRLF warnings on every Rust edit and 21 drifted files, and there is no .editorconfig, rustfmt.toml, deny.toml, pre-commit hook or repack (46.56 MiB loose objects). Smaller debts include an IDE-generated environment.yml with an absolute user path and no notebooks, unignored .claude/ and lobby-screengrab.png litter, eight tracked files embedding C:\Users\cld-main paths, and scripts/tests/test_laya_context.py:617 hard-coding six opponent screen names against CONTRIBUTING.md:69-71. The immediate actions are to make the Python CI lane collect on a clean clone, stop tests writing into the evidence root, and commit the in-flight refactor atomically; the next sprint should purge graphify-out and the PDF, reconcile branches and Dependabot, fix the release allowlist, and replace the "do not commit" handoff culture with a small-commit branch workflow.

## Risk register: technical, product and operational risks with likelihood, impact and mitigation  grade D+ (48/100)
The repository keeps no risk register of its own; risks are implicit in receipt prose, so this is the first ranked one (16 risks, likelihood x impact on 1-5 scales). The top three are all goal-blocking and none has a mitigation path in the repo: (1) the perception ceiling, score 25, where the 256M it1 checkpoint fails its own Gate F (board 0/330 confident at a floor the client pins at 1.0 and can only raise, warm p95 3,027 ms) and the latest 718 s sustained run published only 4 pot-only partial observations; (2) the 5 s decision budget versus 3-4 s inference, score 20, which produced decision-deadline-exceeded on 24 distinct generations in that run (on a target/debug build) and expires 38 of 393 CPU context-lane reads against their 5 s lease; (3) the human-review step, score 20, with 72/72 checklist frames still pending, no owner or date, and every refit/calibration gated behind it. Operational risks are materialising rather than hypothetical: every cargo test run writes synthetic sessions into the private evidence root (850 + 1,363 directories, 5.4 GB, over 100 created today), CI almost certainly cannot collect the Python suite on a clean checkout (bare Python 3.11 runner with no package step versus module-level numpy/PIL imports and a test that exec-loads a gitignored .local file), and the worktree holds a refactor whose modified tracked files import four untracked files, so a plain commit or stash yields a tree that neither compiles nor imports. Product and trust risk comes from contract drift: SECURITY.md and README still promise no images or player names in browser DTOs while HEAD serves capture PNGs on /api/evidence and OCRs names into seat cards, and three active docs deny the Start route that ships. Process risk is concentrated in a single author and AI-session-driven mega-commits (HEAD: 337 files, +559,612 lines, 45.8 MB of generated graph output in a 66.6 MB tracked tree), with HANDOFF.md carrying two contradictory test baselines 130 lines apart. Second-tier risks include the animated-tile suppression window silently stretching from 2 s to 10 s on the 500 ms automatic path with only ignored replay tests, an automatic identity recheck that is vacuous because the supervisor stamps confirmed_at with now_ms(), a release workflow that would sign a bundle whose scripts cannot find laya-pins.json, dual rand majors and a laya 0.1.7 pin that does not match the installed 0.2.0.dev0, a browser that polls at 4 Hz with a fresh TCP connection and re-renders at 10 Hz while labelling yesterday's receipt as current, and a short-stack call-EV defect on the only live decision path. The genuine mitigations are architectural rather than managerial: leases that only shorten, floors that only rise, SHA-256 source witnesses, bounded budgets, loopback-only hardening and a locked pinned toolchain mean the blast radius of nearly every risk above is 'nothing shows', not 'something false shows'. That containment keeps this off an F; the absence of any plan for the three goal-blocking risks, plus active contamination of the evidence base and a probably-red CI, keep it below a C.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, handing the viewer a file to save, or using the viewer's camera, microphone, location, screen or device motion. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). ### A.1 What the page is and how it is built

The Monitor is a dependency-free page with two tabs, Monitor and Reference (`scripts/dashboard/index.html:24-27`). The stdlib `ThreadingHTTPServer` in `scripts/laya-server.py` serves it on loopback. The code is three hand-written files:

- `scripts/dashboard/index.html`: 153 lines.
- `scripts/dashboard/styles.css`: 282 lines.
- `scripts/dashboard/app.js`: 2,858 lines, all in one IIFE.

There is no build step, no package manifest and no lint or type tooling.

How it runs, verified in code:

- **Polling.** It requests `GET /api/state` every 250 ms with one request in flight at most (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:361`). Each request aborts after 1.5 s (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:362`) and is capped at 256 KiB (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:366`). The server answers over HTTP/1.0 with `Connection: close` (`scripts/laya-server.py:860`).
- **Rendering.** All text is written through `textContent`. A 100 ms `setInterval(refreshClocks)` (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2856`) expires leases and re-renders the page.
- **Leases.** Every lane holds a wall-clock and a monotonic deadline. A deadline can only get shorter.
- **Mutations.** The only writes are `POST /api/capture/start|stop`, and they need a control id.
- **Reference.** The Reference text is bundled into `scripts/dashboard/app.js:4-359`, so the tab makes no requests.

**Coverage limits.** The audit ran against a dashboard-only server with no model and no capture. Three paths were therefore verified in code only: provisional values, last-read values and Start/Stop while a request is pending. Screenshots are in `C:/Users/cld-main/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-cld-main-Desktop-github-projects-coinpoker-help/9a033a56-779b-418e-881d-7f600baf0875/scratchpad/shots/`.

Zero is kept distinct from unknown (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:479-486`). The defects below either misstate the page's state or hide its cues; none of them shows a false number.

## GAP: Consumer feed lag (0.5-1.3 s) trips the 1,000 ms freshness check and silently vetoes 12 of 16 d643 partials; where the lag comes from was never found
Why: This run's verifiers refuted readiness claim c4 ("model latency, not the activity gate, is the dominant loss"). Nothing replaced it, so the P0 advice to "cut per-job model latency" may target the wrong layer. I measured the d643 receipts read-only today:
- The Rust child emits capture_health a median 190 ms after capture (max 616).
- The consumer writes the matching ledger row a median 498-1,256 ms after emit, depending on the minute (max 2,100).
- 280 of 517 ledgered heartbeats are fresh_capture=false, although the producer marked all 517 fresh.
- Every one of the 12 dropped partials (generations 34, 39, 103, 105, 106, 148, 153, 174, 177, 178, 181, 182) follows at least one non-fresh heartbeat of the same generation. The 4 admitted ones do not.

The likely mechanism:
- scripts/laya_dashboard.py:1072-1073 judges freshness at consumer time (now - captured < 1000).
- A non-fresh heartbeat calls _invalidate('capture-not-fresh'), which raises invalidated_version (:762-764).
- The partial branch (~:1141-1149) then vetoes the partial with no ledger row.

The same lag reaches the CPU lanes: fast-readouts-live-20261014.summary.json records last_numeric_arrival_lag_ms 1196 with queue lag 4 ms. Nobody has located the sink. Candidates are the supervisor's 100 ms sleep, the fsync'd status.json writes, and the per-row public_snapshot disk reads and lock holds in ManualSessionFeed.ingest_live.

(a) Per-session table. All values were measured from receipts. "Lag" means ledger recorded_utc minus the producer's emitted_at, taken over capture_health rows.

- d643: 16 partials emitted, 4 ledgered (generations 35, 38, 40, 173). Non-fresh: 280 of 516 ledgered capture_health rows (54%). There are 516 ledgered health rows, not 517: the 517th stdout heartbeat falls after ledger max seq 783. Median lag 873 ms (p90 1619 ms), per-minute medians 493–1249 ms. Capture-to-ledger median is 1067 ms.
- d6f4: stdout.jsonl is capped at exactly 20,971,520 bytes, so it covers only the first 5.9 of 15.4 minutes. In that window, 184 partials were emitted and 185 ledgered (about 100%; the extra one is the window edge); 364 are ledgered in total. Non-fresh 0 of 687. Median lag 158 ms (maximum 822 ms).
- ea5a: also capped at 20 MiB, covering 17.6 of 40 minutes. 216 emitted, 217 ledgered (about 100%); 417 ledgered in total. Non-fresh 0 of 2177. Median lag 104 ms (maximum 428 ms). This session has no visual_frame rows.
- Both ledgers are present.

Critic re-verification:
- Partial counts (16 emitted, 4 ledgered) are confirmed.
- "280 of 517" should read 280 of 516 ledgered heartbeats.
- The claim that every dropped partial follows a non-fresh heartbeat is confirmed, with a refinement. All 12 drops had at least one non-fresh heartbeat of the same generation. None of the 4 admitted partials had one. In 3 drops (generations 34, 39, 174), a later fresh heartbeat in the same generation did not restore admission.
- The producer marked all 517 heartbeats fresh. Producer capture-to-emit time was 103–616 ms, so all 280 vetoes would have passed if freshness were judged at emit time.

Veto path in scripts/laya_dashboard.py:
- :1072-1073: fresh requires `now - captured < 1000`, where now is the consumer clock and captured is the producer's capture time.
- :1092-1093: a non-fresh heartbeat calls `_invalidate("capture-not-fresh")`.
- :763-764: `invalidated_version` is raised to the current (gen, epoch). It is only cleared at :683 and :717, which are stream start and reset.
- :942: the partial lease requires `capture["fresh_capture"]`.
- :1139-1149: a missing lease, or `(gen, epoch) <= invalidated_version`, calls `_invalidate` and returns. The ledger write at :1580 is never reached, so the drop leaves only a sequence gap in the ledger.

(b) Lag decomposition. Everything runs synchronously on the supervisor thread, through `on_record` at scripts/laya_capture.py:611.

- **Each supervisor iteration:**
  - Two stat calls (:656).
  - Two Condition-guarded pipe reads (:480-485).
  - Two or three fsync'd status.json writes (:609, :666, :674). Each write is create, write, fsync (:131), ReplaceFileW, and up to four retries of 10 ms (:125-150). Estimated 2–10 ms each (inferred).
  - A check for the STOP file (:683).
  - `time.sleep(0.1)` (:694).
  - Measured: back-to-back rows with no visual_frame between them are spaced a median 85–119 ms apart.
- **Each feed row, through `ingest_live` (laya_dashboard.py:2053-2066):**
  - Two feed-lock acquisitions: `poll` at :1899-1903 and the block at :2056.
  - One or two state-lock acquisitions.
  - Three `public_snapshot` calls (laya_capture.py:303-390). Together these open six files (current.json and status.json, three times) and make about 12 stat or exists checks, plus a glob of the markers directory (:386).
  - No fsync: ledger rows are flushed only (laya_dashboard.py:616-636).
- **Each visual_frame row, in addition (scripts/laya_visual.py):**
  - Reads about 780 KB of PNG plus a SHA-256 hash (:554-555), and up to 4 popup images (:578).
  - Calls `_region_checks` up to three times (:596, :91, :228). Each call decodes two PNGs (:38), so up to six decodes per frame.
  - Measured: each intervening visual_frame adds 350–580 ms to the spacing between rows (zero frames: about 113 ms; one: 465–698 ms; two: 1051 ms).
- **Lock contention:**
  - A background poll runs every 50 ms and takes the feed lock (laya_dashboard.py:2097).
  - `/api/state` (laya-server.py:905-907) calls `ManualSessionFeed.snapshot` (laya_dashboard.py:1843-1880). That holds the feed lock while taking the state lock and the visual, numeric and context locks. The UI polls it every 250 ms (POLL_MS).
- **GIL contention (inferred):** the context lane was busy 84% of the d643 window, with a median of 2.8 s per attempt (measured from .local/laya/events/bd0025…/context.jsonl). Every file read, ctypes call or decode that releases the GIL then waits to get it back.
- **Load correlation (measured):**
  - Median lag by rows emitted in the previous second: 3 rows gives 557 ms, 5 gives 1048 ms, 6 gives 1275 ms (Pearson 0.385).
  - Median lag by perception_diagnostics rows in the previous 5 s: 0 gives 464 ms, 1 gives 634 ms, 2 gives 1141 ms, 3 or more gives 1492 ms (Pearson 0.41).

(c) Verdict: yes, for the partials d643 actually emitted. Consumer lag combined with generation poisoning explains 12 of 12 drops, with perfect separation. Model latency (capture to emit) does not separate the two groups: 1956–3017 ms for dropped partials and 2122–2899 ms for admitted ones. Leases still had at least 1982 ms left when emitted. Two caveats:
- d643's low emission rate (16 in 12 minutes, against 184 in 5.9 minutes for d6f4) is a separate loss upstream that I did not attribute.
- The cost per visual_frame and the GIL contention are inferred from timing gaps. I did not profile them.

Tests: `capture-not-fresh` appears only as UI message strings (test_companion_ui.py:423, :1806, :1815). The health helper sets `emitted = captured = now` (test_laya_dashboard_stage2.py:33-38). The 3000 ms case in test_laya_dashboard.py:537-540 hits the obsolete-record branch (:1059), not the 1000 ms check. stage2:983 only checks that a partial is rejected. No test simulates a capture age of 1000–2499 ms and then expects a partial to be admitted.

(d) Smallest fixes:
1. At :1073, judge freshness at the producer's emit time: `emitted - captured < 1000`. The existing check at :1059 (`now - emitted >= HEARTBEAT_MS`) still bounds delivery delay. This alone would have kept all 280 heartbeats fresh.
2. Stop a non-fresh heartbeat from poisoning its generation:
   - Pass the "capture-not-fresh" invalidation without raising `invalidated_version`, or
   - clear the poisoning when a later fresh heartbeat of the same (gen, epoch) arrives.
   This alone recovers generations 34, 39 and 174.
3. Write a ledger row with the reason before the returns at :1142 and :1149, so vetoes are no longer silent.
4. Cut per-row disk reads:
   - Pass the supervisor's in-memory `status` to `on_record` instead of calling `public_snapshot` three times per row.
   - Skip `poll()` inside `ingest_live`. For sustained sessions it already returns at :1979-1980.
5. Move the PNG read, hashing and region checks off the supervisor thread into the worker queue, and decode each frame once for all three lanes.
6. Write status.json once per iteration, without fsync.

Side finding: the log-limit check at laya_capture.py:656 uses `> MAX_LOG`, but `_write_capped` (:495-500) stops writing at exactly MAX_LOG. The check can therefore never fire. The receipts for d6f4 and ea5a were truncated silently at 20 MiB.

Scratch scripts are in C:/Users/cld-main/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-cld-main-Desktop-github-projects-coinpoker-help/9a033a56-779b-418e-881d-7f600baf0875/scratchpad: lag_gap1.py, lag_gap1_tol.py, service_gap1.py and sess_gap1.py.

## GAP: Why sessions end capture-failed (23 of 49) or feed-failed (7) was never traced to code, and the operator-visible cause was never checked

- The server divides logits by the per-type temperature (laya-server.py:358-360) and rounds each probability to 4 decimals (:366). Pinned choice T = 3.796 (calibration.json temperatures).
- A slot is admitted only when both rank and suit round to 1.0000, so each raw p must be >= 0.99995. At T=3.796, even with every other option tied, that needs a top-1 logit margin >= 43.7 (suit, 6 options) or 47.6 (rank, 15 options).

190	**M4. The docs deny the Start route and name a control that does not exist (effort: small)**
191	
192	- **Lenses:** CON (medium), IA (low).
193	- **Evidence:**
194	  - README.md:51-54, docs/EVENTS_V2.md:267-269 and HANDOFF.md:15-17 all say "Stop capture" and "no HTTP start".
195	  - The page ships "Start monitor" and "Stop monitor" (`scripts/dashboard/index.html:39`), backed by `/api/capture/start` (`scripts/laya-server.py:977`).
196	  - README, HANDOFF and the page give three different launch commands.
197	- **Impact:** Operators look for a control that does not exist, and reviewers miss a route that changes state.
198	- **Fix:**
199	  - Document the route in EVENTS_V2.
200	  - Rename the control in the docs.
201	  - Keep one canonical command.
202	
203	**M5. The recommendation panel is permanently hidden by CSS but still rendered, announced and tested (effort: small)**
204	
205	- **Lenses:** CON (medium), IA, A11Y, ENG (all low).
206	- **Evidence:**
207	  - `.action-panel { display: none; }` (`scripts/dashboard/styles.css:64-65`).
208	  - `renderAction` still fills the panel (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:1935-1951`).
209	  - Screen readers hear "Experimental recommendation available" (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2508`).
210	  - A test asserts "Call" (`scripts/tests/test_companion_ui.py:1018-1023`).
211	  - `#view-label` is also dead (`scripts/dashboard/styles.css:47`, `scripts/dashboard/app.js:2673`).
212	- **Impact:** Screen-reader users are pointed at content that is not on the page, and the tests certify text no one sees.
213	- **Fix:** Decide the intent. Either delete the panel, its announcement and its test, or render it only while advice is live.
214	
215	**M6. Every failure collapses into "Table disconnected" (effort: small)**
216	
217	- **Lenses:** ENG (medium), PERF (medium), SEC (low).
218	- **Evidence:**
219	  - `poll()` treats four different failures the same way (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2630-2637`): schema drift, a network error, a timeout and an oversize body. Nothing records the reason.
220	  - Four live receipts show isolated 2-3.3 s server stalls during healthy capture. Those exceed the 1.5 s timeout. The cause is undetermined.
221	  - Nothing bounds the 42-72 KB snapshot on the server side.
222	- **Impact:** About once per 10-minute session, readings flash to "disconnected", followed by H1's sticky "Stale". A new server enum would also look like a network outage.
223	- **Fix:**
224	  - Disconnect only after two failures in a row.
225	  - Show distinct states for unreachable, timeout and rejected responses, and name the rejected field.
226	  - Bound the snapshot on the server.
227	
228	**M7. Full re-render at 10 Hz, list rebuilds and fixed close-per-request polling (effort: medium)**
229	
230	- **Lenses:** A11Y (medium), IA, ENG, SEC, PERF (all low).
231	- **Evidence:**
232	  - `refreshClocks` re-renders the page every 100 ms (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2608`), plus once per poll (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2584`).
233	  - Four lists are rebuilt with `replaceChildren` and no change check (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2013`, `2293`, `1852`, `2341`). `renderCards` already has such a check.
234	  - The poll stays at 250 ms even when idle (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2639`), and each poll opens a new connection (`scripts/laya-server.py:860`).
235	- **Impact:**
236	  - A screen-reader cursor loses its place up to 10 times a second.
237	  - An idle tab never goes quiet.
238	  - The server handles about 14,400 connections an hour.
239	- **Fix:**
240	  - Add change checks before the four rebuilds.
241	  - Before slowing the tick, add one timer at the earliest lease deadline. Context, visual, numeric and advice leases expire only through this tick today (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2591-2602`).
242	  - Poll adaptively, back off on failure, and use keep-alive.
243	
244	**M8. The test harness cannot see CSS or timers (effort: medium)**
245	
246	- **Lenses:** CON (medium), ENG (medium), PERF (low).
247	- **Evidence:**
248	  - `scripts/tests/test_laya_dashboard_stage2.py:1255` replaces `setInterval` with a no-op.
249	  - Line 1259 of the same file regex-rewrites the source to reach internal functions.
250	  - The DOM shim has no stylesheet.
251	  - README.md:135 and :141 cite "browser checks" that no script in the repo reproduces.
252	  - No test checks poll cadence, payload size or latency.
253	- **Impact:** H2, H3, M1, M3, M5 and M9 are invisible to the 139 passing tests.
254	- **Fix:**
255	  - Add a real-browser smoke test at three viewports that checks computed visibility and overlap.
256	  - Add a latency and size gate over the api.jsonl receipts.
257	
258	**M9. The freshness dot overlaps the seat name at 375 px (effort: trivial)**
259	
260	- **Lenses:** VIS (medium), IA, A11Y, ENG (low).
261	- **Evidence:**
262	  - The dot is absolutely positioned (`scripts/dashboard/styles.css:100`).
263	  - `.seat-select` has no right padding (`scripts/dashboard/styles.css:91`). Only seats with revealed cards reserve space (`scripts/dashboard/styles.css:146`).
264	  - Measured overlap is 9 px.
265	  - 05-mobile-375x812-top.jpg shows the dot over the "g" of "pending" in all six cards.
266	  - The server is loopback-only, so this mainly affects narrow docked windows.
267	- **Impact:** The only per-seat validity cue covers the name it qualifies.
268	- **Fix:** Add `padding-right: 18px`.
269	
270	**M10. Start and Stop disable themselves mid-request and drop focus (effort: small)**
271	
272	- **Lenses:** A11Y (medium).
273	- **Evidence:**
274	  - Both buttons set a controller and then disable themselves (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:626`, `641`, `651`, `668-670`).
275	  - `aria-busy` lands on a disabled button (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:642`).
276	  - Verified in code only.
277	- **Impact:** After pressing Start or Stop, a keyboard or screen-reader operator is dropped at the top of the document.
278	- **Fix:** Use `aria-disabled` plus a guard against repeat clicks.
279	
280	**M11. The live snapshot is built under the feed lock four times a second (effort: medium)**
281	
282	- **Lenses:** PERF (medium).
283	- **Evidence:**
284	  - While holding `self.lock`, `ManualSessionFeed.snapshot()` does two file reads, a full `deepcopy` (`scripts/laya_dashboard.py:1621`), copies of each lane (`scripts/laya_visual.py:857-862`) and a whitespace-formatted `json.dumps` (`scripts/laya-server.py:872`).
285	  - Measured live latency is p50 26-37 ms and p95 83-94 ms.
286	- **Impact:** The page takes CPU and GIL time from inference, and the page and ingest serialize on one lock.
287	- **Fix:**
288	  - Cache the serialized bytes each time the data changes.
289	  - Build the snapshot outside the lock.
290	
291	**M12. Nine hand-rolled lease machines (effort: large)**
292	
293	- **Lenses:** ENG (medium).
294	- **Evidence:**
295	  - Each lane has its own admit, clear and floor logic (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:1260-1297`, `1412-1443`, `1455-1500`, `1855-1880`, `2093-2166`, `2405-2509`).
296	  - Six binding keys are composed differently (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:1262`, `1414`, `1458-1459`, `1856`, `2540-2541`).
297	  - The 1,500 ms and 500 ms values are repeated as bare literals.
298	  - At least one apparent gap is covered elsewhere (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:1263`). That proves the point: intent cannot be read in one place.
299	- **Impact:** A lease bug has to be fixed nine times, and drift cannot be told apart from design.
300	- **Fix:** A single `Lease` type (see A.5).
301	
302	#### Low and nits (condensed table)
303	
304	| Finding | Lenses | Evidence | Fix | Effort |
305	|---|---|---|---|---|
306	| Qualifiers at 9-11 px (12 px is the de facto body size); 17 px summaries; 20 px compact buttons | VIS, A11Y | `scripts/dashboard/styles.css:76`, `95`, `110`, `191` | Raise qualifiers to 12 px and targets to 24 px | trivial |
307	| Five permanent amber badges; "Seat status pending" when nothing is pending; undefined reason terms; the masthead badge wraps at 375 px | IA, CON, VIS | `scripts/dashboard/index.html:30`, `51`, `93`, `100`, `107`; `scripts/dashboard/app.js:1665` | Use a neutral tone for expected states; add a one-line glossary | small |
308	| "Table -" reads as a stray hyphen (the "Phase" label is sr-only) | VIS | `scripts/dashboard/index.html:51`; `scripts/dashboard/app.js:1976` | Hide it when the phase is unknown | trivial |
309	| At 1280 px: a 940 px cap and about 40% of the screen empty; seat cards keep about 29 px reserved but blank | VIS, IA | `scripts/dashboard/styles.css:69`, `91`, `99`; 07-desktop-1280x800.jpg | Use a side rail at 1100 px and above; fill the reserved row | medium |
310	| Control borders at 1.61-1.75:1; dimmed red suit at 3.59:1 | A11Y | `scripts/dashboard/styles.css:3-4`, `12`, `143` | Lighter `--line`; opaque last-read cards | small |
311	| No headings on the two summaries; `aria-label` on generic divs; reference topic changes move no focus; qualifiers exist only in `title` | A11Y | `scripts/dashboard/index.html:35`, `107`, `115`; `scripts/dashboard/app.js:2187-2190`, `2726`, `2733` | Put an h2 inside each summary; focus the article h3; make the text visible | small |
312	| Reference reader runs to about 150 characters per line; the h3 (17 px) is larger than the h2 (14 px) | VIS | `scripts/dashboard/styles.css:22`, `206`, `219-220`; 08-reference-1280x800.jpg | `max-width: 72ch` | trivial |
313	| Global Escape handler acts on the Reference tab; the select's name changes with its value; the count is announced on every keystroke | A11Y | `scripts/dashboard/app.js:2839-2841`; `scripts/dashboard/index.html:109` | Scope Escape and debounce the count | trivial |
314	| Hex literals outside the tokens; dead CSS rules; dense gate predicates; duplicated lookup tables | VIS, ENG | `scripts/dashboard/styles.css:14`, `70-71`, `96`; `scripts/dashboard/app.js:915`, `1198`, `2299-2307` | Tokenize the colours; name the predicates; share the constants | medium |
315	| The reference is inlined while `/api/reference` goes unused; assets are served `no-store` with no ETag | ENG, PERF, CON | `scripts/dashboard/app.js:4-359`; `scripts/laya-server.py:862`, `926-932` | Keep a single source; send an ETag | small |
316	| HEAD and OPTIONS hit the stdlib 501 page without the guard headers; no audit line for capture POSTs; no Sec-Fetch-Site check; no Trusted Types | SEC | `scripts/laya-server.py:687-760`, `856-865`, `884-895`; `scripts/laya_server_validation.py:37-38` | Override `send_error`; add a bounded JSONL log; tighten the CSP | small |
317	| The 300 ms reserve is smaller than poll phase plus p95; `shift()` runs on a 12,000-entry array; `JSON.parse` runs every tick | PERF | README.md:282; `scripts/dashboard/app.js:535-536`, `1748` | Restate the reserve; use a ring buffer | trivial |
318	
319	### A.4 Prioritized fix list (quick wins first, with effort)
320	
321	1. **M1:** drop `sr-only`. Trivial.
322	2. **H4:** tone `#source-status`. Trivial.
323	3. **M9:** pad the seat dot. Trivial.
324	4. **H1:** make the clear reason explicit and add a test. Small.
325	5. **H2 and H3:** visible seat and pot validity, dot shapes, legend. Small.
326	6. **M2:** date the previous session. Small.
327	7. **M3:** "Next step" line, move the lifecycle box out of `<details>`. Small.
328	8. **M5:** decide the recommendation panel and delete the dead UI. Small.
329	9. **M10:** keep focus on Start/Stop. Small.
330	10. **M6:** separate the failure states and require two failures before "disconnected". Small.
331	11. **M7:** change checks, an earliest-deadline timer, adaptive keep-alive polling. Medium.
332	12. **H5 and M4:** reconcile the docs. Small to medium.
333	13. **M8:** real-browser smoke test and latency gate. Medium.
334	14. **M11:** cache the server snapshot. Medium.
335	15. **H6 and M12:** module split, `Lease` type, tooling. Large, about 3-4 days.
336	
337	Items 1-7 touch about 60 lines and remove most of the damage the operator can see.
338	
339	### A.5 Recommended refactor shape
340	
341	Keep the zero-dependency, no-build, strict-CSP design. `script-src 'self'` already allows `<script type="module">`, so the change is only splitting the file and adding the new files to the server's asset map.
342	
343	- **Module layout.**
344	  - `constants.js` and `clock.js`. Inject one `{wall(), mono()}` clock instead of 65 scattered clock calls.
345	  - `dto/*.js`. Normalizers return `{value, reason}`, never a bare `null`.
346	  - `lease.js` and `state.js`.
347	  - `view-model.js`.
348	  - `render/*.js`, plus `net/poll.js` and `main.js`.
349	- **One `Lease` type.**
350	  - It holds `key`, `binding`, `expires`, `deadline`, `closed` and `floor`.
351	  - `admit(candidate, now, rtt)` never renews the same key, closes on a scope boundary and keeps a sequence floor.
352	  - Lanes differ only through a declared `{ttlMs, scopeParts}` table.
353	- **One-way flow.**
354	  - `reduce(state, snapshot, now)` returns the new state plus a `health {healthy, reasons[]}` object.
355	  - `viewModel(state, now)` turns that into strings, tones and validity values.
356	  - Renderers patch the DOM only when their signature changes.
357	  - A dirty flag, coalesced with `requestAnimationFrame`, decides when to render.
358	  - A single timer is set for the earliest lease deadline.
359	- **One visual vocabulary for validity.** Current, provisional, last-read and unknown each get a shape, a colour, an opacity and a visible word. The same treatment applies to seats, pot and board, including under `forced-colors`.
360	- **Tests.**
361	  - Tests import modules directly instead of rewriting the source.
362	  - Pure reducer and lease tests do most of the work.
363	  - A thin real-browser layer checks visibility.
364	  - ESLint and `tsc --checkJs --noEmit` run as dev-only checks.
365	
366	### A.6 Lens scores
367	
368	| Lens | Score /10 | One-line rationale |
369	|---|---|---|
370	| Information architecture and workflow | 5 | The validity machinery is rigorous, but there is no next step, the empty-state message is hidden, the status is green and the "Stale" labels are false. |
371	| Visual design and layout | 6 | Strong palette and an 800x600 fit, undone by colour-only validity, an always-green status and the 375 px overlap. |
372	| Accessibility | 6 | Correct tablist, focus handling and live region; validity is colour-only or absent, lists rebuild at 10 Hz, and Start/Stop drop focus. |
373	| Front-end engineering | 4 | A fail-closed safety floor and 139 tests, inside an untooled 2,858-line IIFE with nine bespoke lease machines. |
374	| Security and robustness | 7 | Strict CSP and verified Host/Origin checks; the DTO contradicts SECURITY.md on names, window metadata and PNGs. |
375	| Runtime performance | 5 | Everything is bounded, but 14 renders a second, close-per-request polling and locked deep copies are wasted work. |
376	| Contract and test fidelity | 6 | Lease semantics are faithful and pinned; five documented UI promises are contradicted, and the harness cannot see CSS. |
377	| Overall (unweighted mean) | 5.6 | The core is trustworthy by construction, but its most important signals do not yet reach the operator. |

## Part A. Frontend appraisal: the Monitor at 127.0.0.1:18090

### A.1 What the page is and how it is built

The Monitor is a dependency-free page with two tabs, Monitor and Reference (`scripts/dashboard/index.html:24-27`). The stdlib `ThreadingHTTPServer` in `scripts/laya-server.py` serves it on loopback. The code is three hand-written files:

- `scripts/dashboard/index.html`: 153 lines.
- `scripts/dashboard/styles.css`: 282 lines.
- `scripts/dashboard/app.js`: 2,858 lines, all in one IIFE.

There is no build step, no package manifest and no lint or type tooling.

How it runs, verified in code:

- **Polling.** It requests `GET /api/state` every 250 ms with one request in flight at most (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:361`). Each request aborts after 1.5 s (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:362`) and is capped at 256 KiB (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:366`). The server answers over HTTP/1.0 with `Connection: close` (`scripts/laya-server.py:860`).
- **Rendering.** All text is written through `textContent`. A 100 ms `setInterval(refreshClocks)` (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2856`) expires leases and re-renders the page.
- **Leases.** Every lane holds a wall-clock and a monotonic deadline. A deadline can only get shorter.
- **Mutations.** The only writes are `POST /api/capture/start|stop`, and they need a control id.
- **Reference.** The Reference text is bundled into `scripts/dashboard/app.js:4-359`, so the tab makes no requests.

**Coverage limits.** The audit ran against a dashboard-only server with no model and no capture. Three paths were therefore verified in code only: provisional values, last-read values and Start/Stop while a request is pending. Screenshots are in `C:/Users/cld-main/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-cld-main-Desktop-github-projects-coinpoker-help/9a033a56-779b-418e-881d-7f600baf0875/scratchpad/shots/`.

**Lens key:** IA (workflow and information architecture), VIS (visual design), A11Y (accessibility), ENG (front-end engineering), SEC (browser/service boundary), PERF (runtime performance), CON (documented contract and tests).

### A.2 What is genuinely good

- **It fails closed.** Nothing renders as current unless it has a source-bound capture and a lease that can only shorten (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2422-2510`). Zero is kept distinct from unknown (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:479-486`). The defects below either misstate the page's state or hide its cues; none of them shows a false number.
- **The boundary is hardened, and this was verified live.**
  - Strict CSP, nosniff and no-referrer headers (`scripts/laya_server_validation.py:37-38`).
  - Host and Origin allowlists. They rejected a foreign Host, a missing Host, `Origin: null` and a duplicated Host (`scripts/laya-server.py:884-895`).
  - No HTML-string sinks anywhere.
  - Response reads are bounded (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:575-614`).
  - Server data is validated against closed vocabularies and checked against the expected capture scope (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:942-981`).
- **The accessibility foundations are real.**
  - A skip link (`scripts/dashboard/index.html:14`).
  - A roving-tabindex tablist (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2821-2836`).
  - Focus moves into player details and returns from them (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:1546`, `1724-1730`).
  - The live region de-duplicates announcements (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:569-573`).
  - Cards are `role="img"` and carry provenance in their names (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:1215-1226`).
  - Text contrast is 7.2:1 or better.
  - A DOM probe showed that the Reference topic buttons do have accessible names.
- **The layout fits the target window.** A subgrid table sits over an isolated SVG (`scripts/dashboard/styles.css:69-87`). It fits status, controls, six seats, board and pot at 800x600 with no scrolling (02-clean-load-800x600.jpg). It reflows to two columns at 375 px without horizontal overflow.
- **The visible copy is honest.**
  - "A dash is unknown" (`scripts/dashboard/index.html:122`).
  - The board dims last-seen cards and says so (`scripts/dashboard/styles.css:143`, `scripts/dashboard/app.js:1632`). This is the pattern the seats should copy.
- **It is passive and well tested.**
  - Suspend and resume never start capture (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2643-2661`).
  - 139 Node-driven tests pin the lease semantics (for example `scripts/tests/test_companion_ui.py:1396`, `1771`).
  - The bundled reference is parity-tested (`scripts/tests/test_poker_reference.py:245`).

### A.3 Findings

#### Critical / High

There are no critical findings.

**H1. One failed poll leaves never-read fields labelled "Stale" (effort: small)**

- **Lenses:** IA (high), ENG (high), SEC (medium), CON (medium). PERF's stall finding (M6) is what triggers it.
- **Evidence:**
  - `disconnected()` calls `clearObservation("stale")` (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2371-2378`).
  - That function's default parameter is the stored `clearReason` (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2358-2359`), so the stale reason is persisted.
  - The `observation: null` path and `resume()` call it with no argument (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2425`, `2658`), which keeps "stale".
  - Only a successful admission resets the reason (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2501`).
  - `reasonFor()` then returns "Stale" (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:504-508`), and Diagnostics shows "Reading expired" (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2202`).
  - Seen live: 01-first-load-sticky-stale-800x600.jpg shows "Stale" under the pot and "Unknown / Stale" on the board. 02-clean-load-800x600.jpg shows "Insufficient context" instead.
  - Every tab hide and show takes the same path. The existing harness could catch this, but no test does.
- **Impact:** After any timeout or tab switch, the operator is told a reading existed and then expired, when nothing was ever admitted.
- **Fix:**
  - Pass "stale" only when a lease was actually active; the `wasActive` value at `scripts/dashboard/app.js:2360` already holds this.
  - Require an explicit reason at every call.
  - Add a test: a failed poll followed by an idle snapshot must show "Insufficient context".

**H2. Seat validity is shown only by colour and a 7 px dot; "Last read" labels are clipped (effort: small)**

- **Lenses:** IA (high), VIS (high), A11Y (high, plus a low finding on forced colours), CON (HANDOFF wording, low).
- **Evidence:**
  - `retainedLabel()` writes "Last read / Awaiting recheck | Source changed" into each seat's reason field (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:1555`, `1702`, `1927`). `scripts/dashboard/styles.css:106` clips that field to 1x1 px. Only the pot reason stays visible (`scripts/dashboard/styles.css:76`).
  - The freshness text (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:1715-1716`) is shrunk into a dot with `font-size: 0` (`scripts/dashboard/styles.css:100`).
  - A last-read dot looks the same as an unknown dot (`scripts/dashboard/styles.css:103`).
  - The mint and amber fills differ by only 1.09:1.
  - The rest of the cue is text colour (`scripts/dashboard/styles.css:117-118`, `158`). It reuses the grey of the labels and dashes.
  - There is no legend.
  - The forced-colours block (`scripts/dashboard/styles.css:279-282`) does not restore the fills.
  - HANDOFF.md:59-60 claims "unmistakable" labels, in wording the code does not use.
- **Impact:** A stale stack is just a greyer number, and its dot matches a seat that was never read. This fails WCAG 1.4.1 on the exact distinction the page exists to show.
- **Fix:**
  - Show the reason and freshness text in the reserved, empty `.seat-markers` row (`scripts/dashboard/styles.css:99`).
  - Give each state its own dot shape.
  - Dim last-read values the way the board dims last-seen cards.
  - Add a legend.
  - Align HANDOFF.md with the shipped labels.

**H3. A provisional CPU-read pot looks identical to an admitted pot (effort: small)**

- **Lenses:** A11Y (high).
- **Evidence:**
  - `scripts/dashboard/app.js:1993-1999` writes the numeric lane's pot with normal classes and sets only `data-reading="provisional"`. It also blanks `#pot-reason`.
  - No CSS selector targets that attribute on the pot. The provisional styling is scoped to seats (`scripts/dashboard/styles.css:117-118`).
  - The tests check only the dataset value (`scripts/tests/test_laya_numeric_ui.py:20`).
- **Impact:** The largest number on the table can be an unvalidated read with a 1.5 s lease, shown with no visible or spoken qualifier.
- **Fix:**
  - Show a visible "Provisional / CPU read" reason.
  - Add a dashed amber style for the provisional pot.
  - Link the reason with `aria-describedby`.
  - Test the reason text.

**H4. The status word is always the success colour, even for "Disconnected" (effort: trivial)**

- **Lenses:** VIS (high), IA (medium).
- **Evidence:**
  - `scripts/dashboard/styles.css:49` sets `#source-status { color: var(--mint); }` unconditionally. Mint is the page's "okay" tone (`scripts/dashboard/styles.css:41`).
  - `renderSource` writes "Disconnected", "Session stopped" and "Session status stale" with `text()`, never with `status()`, so no tone is ever set (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2180-2185`, `564`).
  - The computed colour was green in 02-clean-load-800x600.jpg and in 05-mobile-375x812-top.jpg.
- **Impact:** The one at-a-glance colour cue signals health exactly when the feed is down. Combined with M1, a dropped feed has no visible amber or red cue at all.
- **Fix:**
  - Delete the rule.
  - Set the tone in `renderSource`: okay, warning or danger.
  - Assert the tone after `disconnected()`.

**H5. Opponent names, popup window metadata and capture PNGs reach the browser, contrary to SECURITY.md (effort: medium)**

- **Lenses:** CON (high), SEC (medium for the DTO, low for the evidence route).
- **Evidence:**
  - Seat identity is the OCR'd on-screen name (`scripts/laya_context.py:633`). The page renders it in seat cards and in the player panel next to the client's VPIP/PFR (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:1660-1668`, `1732-1771`).
  - `normalizeCaptureRef` keeps the popup's `hwnd`, `process_id` and `window_class` (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:942-963`). That data is written into `data-capture-ref` on DOM nodes (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:526-541`).
  - `/api/evidence/<sha256>` serves original PNGs (`scripts/laya-server.py:918-925`).
  - The evidence link has no `target` (`scripts/dashboard/index.html:69`), so clicking it navigates the Monitor away and stops polling.

194	### B.5 Security, privacy and licensing
195	
196	**Strengths (verified in code).**
197	- Host and Origin headers are checked before any route runs (`scripts/laya-server.py:884-895`).
198	- GET and POST responses send a deny-by-default content security policy (CSP) plus nosniff, no-referrer and no-store (`scripts/laya-server.py:856-864`, `scripts/laya_server_validation.py:37`).
199	- Static assets come from a three-entry dict, so path traversal is not possible (`scripts/laya-server.py:935-942`).
200	- Request bodies are capped, and requests are not logged (`scripts/laya-server.py:853`).
201	- The Rust client accepts only loopback endpoints and does not follow redirects (`crates/ingest/src/vlm.rs:146-182`, `bin/config.rs:311-318`).
202	- `app.js` never builds HTML from strings.
203	- Model weights are untracked, and their CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 license is recorded (`MODEL_LICENSES.md:36-40`).
204	
205	**Weaknesses.**
206	- **Privacy claims are contradicted by code.** `SECURITY.md:23-25` and `:38`, `README.md:122-123` and `:132`, and `docs/EVENTS_V2.md:161` say images, player names and window/process IDs never reach the browser. The code does all three:
207	  - `/api/evidence/<sha256>` returns full capture PNGs (`scripts/laya-server.py:918-925`, `scripts/laya_visual.py:359`, `369`).
208	  - Player names read by OCR go into the seat cards (`scripts/laya_visual.py:400`, `scripts/dashboard/app.js:1041-1044`, `1664-1666`).
209	  - Popup window handles and process IDs are sent to the page (`scripts/laya_visual.py:277`, `app.js:953-961`).
210	- **Real screen names in a tracked file.** Six apparent real screen names are hard-coded in `scripts/tests/test_laya_context.py:617`. CONTRIBUTING.md:69-71 forbids this, and the names are already pushed.
211	- **Third-party files without a notice.** A 16.5 MB third-party PDF and two reference images are committed with no license notice.
212	- **Untrusted HTTP methods skip the hardening.** HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT and DELETE fall through to the standard-library error page without the hardening headers; only `do_GET` and `do_POST` are defined (`scripts/laya-server.py:897`, `946`).
213	- **The local listener is unauthenticated.** Any local process can start capture or occupy the GPU.
214	- **Supply chain.** CI runs no cargo-audit, cargo-deny or pip-audit, and Python packages are pinned by version only, with no hashes.
215	- **Machine paths in tracked files.** Absolute paths from the author's machine appear in `environment.yml:7`, `HANDOFF.md:4` and seven `.kilo` plans.
216	- **The public default branch shows the old product.** `origin/main` (4a91af9) still has the remote-model option, port 8080, and a WebSocket mirror that skips Origin and Host checks (origin/main `crates/ui/src/ws.rs:131-155`).
